1	# DMLS — Deb's Minimal Life Simulator
2	
3	> *A minimal life simulation engine. Maximal engineering underneath.*
4	
5	DMLS is a 2D life simulation built on a declarative relational engine (Epilog), a generative spatial layer (Perlin noise, seeded PRNG), and a Raylib renderer written in Odin. Characters live on a 256×256 grid, form relationships, develop crushes, build rivalries — and you watch it unfold from outside.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Stack
10	
11	| Layer | Technology | Role |
12	|-------|-----------|------|
13	| Relational engine | Epilog v0.2 (C++23) | Fact storage, relationship queries, derived logic |
14	| Simulation & rendering | Odin + Raylib | Game loop, grid, noise, randomness, UI |
15	| Bridge | `extern "C"` API + Odin `foreign` | Epilog embedded as a C++ module |
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Architecture Overview
20	
21	```
22	┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
23	│               Raylib Window             │
24	│  ┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
25	│  │  Simulation View │  Stats Panel    │ │
26	│  │  (RenderTexture) │  (RenderTexture)│ │
27	│  └──────────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
28	└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
29	            ↕ Odin game loop
30	┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
31	│           Odin Simulation Layer         │
32	│  Grid · Noise · Randomness · Characters │
33	│  Character Creation · System Manager   │
34	└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
35	            ↕ C++↔Odin bridge
36	┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
37	│         Epilog v0.2 (C++ module)        │
38	│  Facts · Rules · Queries · Memoization  │
39	└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
40	```
41	
42	---
43	
44	## Phase 0: Epilog v0.2 (Prerequisite)
45	
46	Complete the relational engine before DMLS begins.
47	
48	### Tasks
49	
50	- [ ] First-argument indexing
51	  - Hash clauses by functor/value of first argument
52	  - Skip non-matching clauses without attempting unification
53	  - Fast path for ground fact lookup vs rule resolution
54	
55	- [ ] Memoization cache
56	  - Cache results of pure (side-effect-free) subgoals
57	  - Invalidate on `assert`/`retract`
58	  - Do not cache predicates with side effects (`write`, `nl`)
59	
60	- [ ] Embedding API (`extern "C"`)
61	  - `epilog_init()` — initialise all arenas and tables
62	  - `epilog_assert(fact: *c_char)` — assert a fact string
63	  - `epilog_retract(fact: *c_char)` — retract a matching fact
64	  - `epilog_query_bool(goal: *c_char) -> bool` — yes/no query
65	  - `epilog_query_bindings(goal: *c_char) -> EpilogResult*` — return variable bindings
66	  - `epilog_free_result(result: EpilogResult*)` — release result memory
67	  - `epilog_shutdown()` — tear down cleanly
68	
69	- [ ] Copy source to `dmls/engine/epilog/` as self-contained module
70	
71	### Acceptance Criteria
72	
73	```prolog
74	crushing(uriel, character_a).
75	crushing(anna_croft, character_a).
76	rivals(X, Y) :- crushing(X, Z), crushing(Y, Z), X \= Y.
77	?- rivals(uriel, anna_croft).   % true
78	?- rivals(X, character_a).        % fail — character_a has no crush
79	```
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Phase 1: Project Skeleton
84	
85	Stand up the Odin project and confirm the bridge works end-to-end.
86	
87	### Tasks
88	
89	- [ ] Directory structure
90	
91	```
92	dmls/
93	├── engine/
94	│   └── epilog/          Epilog v0.2 C++ source (copied module)
95	├── src/
96	│   ├── main.odin        Entry point
97	│   ├── bridge.odin      foreign import of Epilog C API
98	│   ├── sim/             Simulation systems
99	│   ├── render/          Raylib rendering layer
100	│   ├── ui/              Character creation, stats panel
101	│   └── data/            Save/load, binary format
102	├── assets/              Sprites, fonts, icons
103	├── build.sh / build.bat
104	└── DMLS_PLAN.md
105	```
106	
107	- [ ] Build system
108	  - Compile Epilog to `epilog.a` / `epilog.lib`
109	  - Odin build links against it via `foreign import`
110	  - Single build script for Linux and Windows
111	
112	- [ ] Bridge smoke test
113	  - Assert a fact from Odin, query it back, confirm result
114	  - Confirm `epilog_query_bindings` returns correct variable values
115	
116	---
117	
118	## Phase 2: Character Creation Screen
119	
120	Characters must exist before the simulation means anything.
121	
122	### Character Data
123	
124	```odin
125	Character :: struct {
126	    id          : u32,
127	    name        : string,
128	    nickname    : string,         // what others call them
129	    age         : u8,
130	    gender      : Gender,
131	    dating_pref : DatingPref,
132	    personality : Personality,    // e.g. Ambitious_Achiever
133	    pronouns    : Pronouns,
134	    position    : [2]i32,         // grid cell
135	    sprite      : u32,            // sprite index
136	}
137	```
138	
139	### Tasks
140	
141	- [ ] Character creation UI
142	  - Name and nickname input fields
143	  - Age, gender, dating preference selectors
144	  - Personality type picker (Ambitious, Outgoing, etc.)
145	  - Pronoun selector
146	  - Sprite selector (palette-swappable base sprites)
147	  - Confirm screen — "Does everything look good?"
148	
149	- [ ] Relationship seeding screen
150	  - After creating a character, optionally tag existing residents
151	  - Tags: Friend, Sibling, Stranger, Partner (pre-seeds Epilog facts)
152	
153	- [ ] Assert character into Epilog on creation
154	  - `character(id, name, personality)`
155	  - `dating_pref(id, male)` / `dating_pref(id, female)` / `dating_pref(id, any)`
156	  - `relationship(id_a, id_b, friend)` etc.
157	
158	- [ ] Resident list screen
159	  - View all current island residents
160	  - Select to inspect relationship graph
161	
162	---
163	
164	## Phase 3: Grid and World
165	
166	The spatial layer the simulation lives on.
167	
168	### Tasks
169	
170	- [ ] 256×256 grid
171	  - Each cell stores: terrain type, occupant ID (or empty), object ID
172	  - Grid rendered as the simulation view (left RenderTexture)
173	
174	- [ ] Perlin noise terrain generation
175	  - Implement or port a minimal Perlin noise generator in Odin
176	  - Generate terrain at world creation: beach, grass, town, forest zones
177	  - Seed-reproducible — same seed = same island
178	
179	- [ ] World seed system
180	  - World seed stored in save file header
181	  - Displayed on stats panel
182	  - Can be entered manually at world creation
183	
184	- [ ] Character placement
185	  - Spawn characters at valid grid positions (town/grass zones)
186	  - Characters wander autonomously each tick within their zone
187	
188	---
189	
190	## Phase 4: Randomness Systems
191	
192	Two independent randomness axes — spatial/generative and social/event-driven.
193	
194	### Independent Randomness
195	Pure draws with no memory. Used for: terrain events, item drops, idle animations.
196	
197	```odin
198	independent_rand :: proc(seed: u64) -> f64 { ... }
199	```
200	
201	### Dependent Randomness
202	Seeded chains where one outcome influences the next. Used for: relationship progression, mood shifts, crush development.
203	
204	```odin
205	DependentRNG :: struct {
206	    state : u64,
207	    seq   : u64,
208	}
209	
210	dependent_next :: proc(rng: ^DependentRNG) -> f64 { ... }
211	```
212	
213	### Weighted Randomness
214	Draw from a distribution. Used for: personality assignment, event selection.
215	
216	```odin
217	weighted_choice :: proc(options: []string, weights: []f64) -> string { ... }
218	```
219	
220	### Non-weighted Randomness
221	Uniform draw from a set. Used for: idle dialogue, sprite variation.
222	
223	### Tasks
224	
225	- [ ] Implement all four randomness modes in `src/sim/rand.odin`
226	- [ ] Expose seed state for save/load
227	- [ ] Confirm dependent RNG produces identical sequences from same seed
228	
229	---
230	
231	## Phase 5: Relational Simulation
232	
233	The Epilog-powered social layer.
234	
235	### Relationship Facts
236	
237	```prolog
238	character(deb, ambitious_achiever).
239	character(uriel, outgoing_merrymaker).
240	character(anna, outgoing_dynamo).
241	
242	crushing(uriel, deb).
243	friend(deb, uriel).
244	acquaintance(anna, deb).
245	stranger(anna, uriel).
246	sibling(saloni, deb).
247	```
248	
249	### Derived Rules
250	
251	```prolog
252	rivals(X, Y) :-
253	    crushing(X, Z),
254	    crushing(Y, Z),
255	    X \= Y.
256	
257	eligible(X, Y) :-
258	    dating_pref(X, Pref),
259	    gender(Y, Pref),
260	    \+ partner(X, _),
261	    \+ sibling(X, Y).
262	
263	best_friends(X, Y) :-
264	    friend(X, Y),
265	    friend(Y, X),
266	    interaction_count(X, Y, N),
267	    N > 10.
268	```
269	
270	### Tasks
271	
272	- [ ] Define base fact schema (character, relationship, interaction_count, mood)
273	- [ ] Write derived rules for: rivals, eligible, best_friends, unrequited
274	- [ ] Tick system — every N real seconds = 1 simulation tick
275	  - Characters near each other increment `interaction_count`
276	  - Dependent RNG decides if a crush develops this tick
277	  - Query `eligible(X, Y)` before allowing crush to form
278	  - Assert new crush facts, retract stale ones
279	
280	- [ ] Crush resolution
281	  - If a character develops two crushes, surface a player prompt
282	  - Player chooses — losing crush relationship unchanged
283	  - Reflects the Tomodachi Life mechanic accurately
284	
285	- [ ] Mood system
286	  - Each character has a mood: happy, content, sad, lovestruck, jealous
287	  - Derived from relationship state each tick
288	  - `mood(X, jealous) :- rivals(X, _).`
289	
290	---
291	
292	## Phase 6: Rendering
293	
294	Two RenderTextures composited onto a single Raylib window.
295	
296	### Layout
297	
298	```
299	┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
300	│  DMLS — Yggdrasilz                        [seed: ...]│
301	├─────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┤
302	│                             │  ISLAND STATS          │
303	│     Simulation View         │  Residents: 4          │
304	│     (256×256 grid)          │  Active crushes: 2     │
305	│                             │  Rival pairs: 1        │
306	│                             │  Tick: 00:04:32        │
307	│                             │─────────────────────── │
308	│                             │  RELATIONSHIPS         │
309	│                             │  uriel → deb [crush]   │
310	│                             │  anna ↔ deb [acquaint] │
311	│                             │  deb ↔ saloni [sibling]│
312	│                             │─────────────────────── │
313	│                             │  EVENTS                │
314	│                             │  [04:31] uriel stares  │
315	│                             │  [04:28] anna & deb    │
316	│                             │  trade stories         │
317	└─────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘
318	```
319	
320	### Tasks
321	
322	- [ ] Two `RenderTexture2D` — simulation and stats panel
323	- [ ] Simulation view: grid tiles, character sprites, relationship arrows on hover
324	- [ ] Stats panel: resident list, active crushes, rival pairs, event log, tick counter
325	- [ ] Event log — rolling last 10 social events (crush formed, rivals detected, mood change)
326	- [ ] Hover inspect — click a character to see their full relationship list
327	- [ ] Update rates: simulation at 60fps, stats panel at 10fps
328	
329	---
330	
331	## Phase 7: Save and Load
332	
333	### Binary Save Format
334	
335	```
336	[4 bytes]  Magic: "DMLS"
337	[4 bytes]  Version: u32
338	[8 bytes]  World seed: u64
339	[4 bytes]  Tick count: u32
340	[4 bytes]  Character count: u32
341	[N bytes]  Character records (fixed-size structs)
342	[4 bytes]  Fact count: u32
343	[N bytes]  Epilog fact strings (length-prefixed)
344	[4 bytes]  Event log entry count: u32
345	[N bytes]  Event log entries (length-prefixed strings)
346	[4 bytes]  Checksum: CRC32
347	```
348	
349	### Tasks
350	
351	- [ ] Serialise grid state to binary
352	- [ ] Serialise all current Epilog facts as strings (via `write/1` dump)
353	- [ ] Serialise dependent RNG state (seed + sequence counter)
354	- [ ] Deserialise on load — re-assert all facts into fresh Epilog instance
355	- [ ] CRC32 checksum validation on load
356	- [ ] Auto-save every 60 ticks
357	
358	---
359	
360	## Phase 8: Polish
361	
362	- [ ] Title screen with world name input and seed entry
363	- [ ] Island naming screen ("Yggdrasilz")
364	- [ ] Relationship event cutscenes (simple sprite animation overlay)
365	- [ ] Idle animations per personality type
366	- [ ] Sound effects via Raylib audio (optional)
367	- [ ] README and build instructions
368	
369	---
370	
371	## Milestones
372	
373	| Milestone | Deliverable |
374	|-----------|-------------|
375	| M0 | Epilog v0.2 complete, embedding API working |
376	| M1 | Odin skeleton, bridge smoke test passing |
377	| M2 | Character creation screen end-to-end |
378	| M3 | 256×256 grid with Perlin noise rendering |
379	| M4 | Randomness systems implemented and tested |
380	| M5 | Relational simulation running — crushes, rivals, moods |
381	| M6 | Dual RenderTexture layout with stats panel |
382	| M7 | Save/load working with full state round-trip |
383	| M8 | Polish pass — title screen, animations, release build |
384	
385	---
386	
387	## Core Invariant
388	
389	> The Epilog engine is always the source of truth for social state.
390	> Odin never caches relationship data — it queries Epilog every tick.
391	> Rendering reflects queries, never assumptions.
392	
393	---
394	
395	*Named for the island. Built for the drama.*

# DMLS — Deb's Minimal Life Simulator

> *A minimal life simulation engine. Maximal engineering underneath.*

DMLS is a 2D life simulation built on a declarative relational engine (Epilog), a generative spatial layer (Perlin noise, seeded PRNG), and a Raylib renderer written in Odin. Characters live on a 256×256 grid, form relationships, develop crushes, build rivalries — and you watch it unfold from outside.

---

## Stack

| Layer | Technology | Role |
|-------|-----------|------|
| Relational engine | Epilog v0.2 (C++23) | Fact storage, relationship queries, derived logic |
| Simulation & rendering | Odin + Raylib | Game loop, grid, noise, randomness, UI |
| Bridge | `extern "C"` API + Odin `foreign` | Epilog embedded as a C++ module |

---

## Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               Raylib Window             │
│  ┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Simulation View │  Stats Panel    │ │
│  │  (RenderTexture) │  (RenderTexture)│ │
│  └──────────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ Odin game loop
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           Odin Simulation Layer         │
│  Grid · Noise · Randomness · Characters │
│  Character Creation · System Manager   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ C++↔Odin bridge
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         Epilog v0.2 (C++ module)        │
│  Facts · Rules · Queries · Memoization  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Phase 0: Epilog v0.2 (Prerequisite)

Complete the relational engine before DMLS begins.

### Tasks

- [ ] First-argument indexing
  - Hash clauses by functor/value of first argument
  - Skip non-matching clauses without attempting unification
  - Fast path for ground fact lookup vs rule resolution

- [ ] Memoization cache
  - Cache results of pure (side-effect-free) subgoals
  - Invalidate on `assert`/`retract`
  - Do not cache predicates with side effects (`write`, `nl`)

- [ ] Embedding API (`extern "C"`)
  - `epilog_init()` — initialise all arenas and tables
  - `epilog_assert(fact: *c_char)` — assert a fact string
  - `epilog_retract(fact: *c_char)` — retract a matching fact
  - `epilog_query_bool(goal: *c_char) -> bool` — yes/no query
  - `epilog_query_bindings(goal: *c_char) -> EpilogResult*` — return variable bindings
  - `epilog_free_result(result: EpilogResult*)` — release result memory
  - `epilog_shutdown()` — tear down cleanly

- [ ] Copy source to `dmls/engine/epilog/` as self-contained module

### Acceptance Criteria

```prolog
crushing(uriel, character_a).
crushing(anna_croft, character_a).
rivals(X, Y) :- crushing(X, Z), crushing(Y, Z), X \= Y.
?- rivals(uriel, anna_croft).   % true
?- rivals(X, character_a).        % fail — character_a has no crush
```

---

## Phase 1: Project Skeleton

Stand up the Odin project and confirm the bridge works end-to-end.

### Tasks

- [ ] Directory structure

```
dmls/
├── engine/
│   └── epilog/          Epilog v0.2 C++ source (copied module)
├── src/
│   ├── main.odin        Entry point
│   ├── bridge.odin      foreign import of Epilog C API
│   ├── sim/             Simulation systems
│   ├── render/          Raylib rendering layer
│   ├── ui/              Character creation, stats panel
│   └── data/            Save/load, binary format
├── assets/              Sprites, fonts, icons
├── build.sh / build.bat
└── DMLS_PLAN.md
```

- [ ] Build system
  - Compile Epilog to `epilog.a` / `epilog.lib`
  - Odin build links against it via `foreign import`
  - Single build script for Linux and Windows

- [ ] Bridge smoke test
  - Assert a fact from Odin, query it back, confirm result
  - Confirm `epilog_query_bindings` returns correct variable values

---

## Phase 2: Character Creation Screen

Characters must exist before the simulation means anything.

### Character Data

```odin
Character :: struct {
    id          : u32,
    name        : string,
    nickname    : string,         // what others call them
    age         : u8,
    gender      : Gender,
    dating_pref : DatingPref,
    personality : Personality,    // e.g. Ambitious_Achiever
    pronouns    : Pronouns,
    position    : [2]i32,         // grid cell
    sprite      : u32,            // sprite index
}
```

### Tasks

- [ ] Character creation UI
  - Name and nickname input fields
  - Age, gender, dating preference selectors
  - Personality type picker (Ambitious, Outgoing, etc.)
  - Pronoun selector
  - Sprite selector (palette-swappable base sprites)
  - Confirm screen — "Does everything look good?"

- [ ] Relationship seeding screen
  - After creating a character, optionally tag existing residents
  - Tags: Friend, Sibling, Stranger, Partner (pre-seeds Epilog facts)

- [ ] Assert character into Epilog on creation
  - `character(id, name, personality)`
  - `dating_pref(id, male)` / `dating_pref(id, female)` / `dating_pref(id, any)`
  - `relationship(id_a, id_b, friend)` etc.

- [ ] Resident list screen
  - View all current island residents
  - Select to inspect relationship graph

---

## Phase 3: Grid and World

The spatial layer the simulation lives on.

### Tasks

- [ ] 256×256 grid
  - Each cell stores: terrain type, occupant ID (or empty), object ID
  - Grid rendered as the simulation view (left RenderTexture)

- [ ] Perlin noise terrain generation
  - Implement or port a minimal Perlin noise generator in Odin

Two independent randomness axes — spatial/generative and social/event-driven.

### Independent Randomness
Pure draws with no memory. Used for: terrain events, item drops, idle animations.

```odin
independent_rand :: proc(seed: u64) -> f64 { ... }
```

### Dependent Randomness
Seeded chains where one outcome influences the next. Used for: relationship progression, mood shifts, crush development.

```odin
DependentRNG :: struct {
    state : u64,
    seq   : u64,
}

dependent_next :: proc(rng: ^DependentRNG) -> f64 { ... }
```

### Weighted Randomness
Draw from a distribution. Used for: personality assignment, event selection.

```odin
weighted_choice :: proc(options: []string, weights: []f64) -> string { ... }
```

### Non-weighted Randomness
Uniform draw from a set. Used for: idle dialogue, sprite variation.

character(anna, outgoing_dynamo).

friend(deb, uriel).
acquaintance(anna, deb).
stranger(anna, uriel).
sibling(saloni, deb).

rivals(X, Y) :-

    crushing(Y, Z),

eligible(X, Y) :-

    gender(Y, Pref),

1	/*
2	 * epilog_ffi.h — C-linkage public API for the Epilog inference engine.
3	 *
4	 * This header is pure C (C99+) and intentionally exposes no C++ types.
5	 * Consumers: C, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, and any other language that
6	 * can load a shared library and call C ABI functions.
7	 *
8	 * Lifecycle
9	 * ---------
10	 *   1. epilog_create()          — allocate + init an engine instance
11	 *   2. epilog_load_string()     — add Prolog facts/rules from a source string
12	 *   3. epilog_query()           — run a query; iterate via callback
13	 *   4. epilog_destroy()         — free all resources
14	 *
15	 * Thread safety
16	 * -------------
17	 *   Each EpilogEngine is independent.  Do NOT share one instance across
18	 *   threads concurrently.  Multiple instances in separate threads is fine.
19	 *
20	 * Error codes
21	 * -----------
22	 *   All functions that can fail return int.
23	 *   0  = success
24	 *  -1  = general error / bad argument
25	 *  -2  = capacity overflow (too many facts, atoms, etc.)
26	 *  -3  = parse error
27	 *
28	 * Solution callback
29	 * -----------------
30	 *   epilog_query() calls your callback once per solution.
31	 *   Return EPILOG_NEXT to ask for the next solution.
32	 *   Return EPILOG_STOP to stop early (like Prolog's !).
33	 *
34	 * Term inspection
35	 * ---------------
36	 *   Inside the callback, use epilog_soln_* to inspect bound values.
37	 *   EpilogVarIter lets you walk over the variables in the query.
38	 */
39	
40	#ifndef EPILOG_FFI_H
41	#define EPILOG_FFI_H
42	
43	#include <stdint.h>
44	#include <stddef.h>
45	
46	#ifdef __cplusplus
47	extern "C" {
48	#endif
49	
50	/* ---- Opaque engine handle ------------------------------------------------ */
51	
52	typedef struct EpilogEngine EpilogEngine;
53	
54	/* ---- Callback return codes ----------------------------------------------- */
55	
56	typedef enum EpilogSignal {
57	    EPILOG_NEXT = 0,   /* continue: ask for more solutions */
58	    EPILOG_STOP = 1    /* stop: do not produce further solutions */
59	} EpilogSignal;
60	
61	/* ---- Term kinds ----------------------------------------------------------- */
62	
63	typedef enum EpilogTermKind {
64	    EPILOG_TERM_ATOM     = 1,
65	    EPILOG_TERM_VAR      = 2,
66	    EPILOG_TERM_COMPOUND = 3,
67	    EPILOG_TERM_INT      = 4,
68	    EPILOG_TERM_UNBOUND  = 5   /* variable with no binding */
69	} EpilogTermKind;

72	
73	typedef struct EpilogSolution EpilogSolution;

76

78	 * EpilogCallback — called once per solution.
79	 *

81	 *   userdata — the pointer you passed to epilog_query()
82	 *
83	 * Return EPILOG_NEXT to request the next solution, EPILOG_STOP to halt.
84	 */

86	                                       void                 *userdata);

89	
90	/*

92	 * Returns nullptr on allocation failure (extremely unlikely given static arenas).
93	 */
94	EpilogEngine *epilog_create(void);

97	void epilog_destroy(EpilogEngine *engine);

100

103	 *

105	 *

107	 */

111

114	 *
115	 *   goal_src — NUL-terminated goal string WITHOUT the "?- " prefix and
116	 *              WITHOUT the trailing ".".  Examples:
117	 *                  "grandparent(alice, carol)"

120	 *   userdata — passed unchanged to cb

123	 */

131	 */

136	 * Returns nullptr if i is out of range.

138	 */

content.content:
# Epilog

A modern logic programming runtime inspired by Prolog, designed for multicore systems, incremental reasoning, and predictive execution.

## Project Overview

Epilog is not a Prolog rewrite — it is the next evolutionary step after Prolog. It preserves the elegance of logic programming (facts, rules, unification, backtracking) while reimagining the execution engine for modern hardware: multicore CPUs, large datasets, incremental computation, and database-backed fact storage.

## Core Invariants

- **Logic is truth.** Predictions, caching, and speculative execution never alter facts, rules, or logical conclusions. They affect only speed and scheduling.
- **Reactive reasoning.** Epilog tracks dependencies between facts, rules, and conclusions. When a fact changes, only impacted nodes recompute — not the entire reasoning graph.
- **Multicore first.** Parallelism is a fundamental feature, not an afterthought. Branch exploration, cache generation, and rule evaluation should exploit all available cores.
- **Database native.** Facts are not limited to memory. The inference engine is a reasoning layer over external data sources (SQLite, PostgreSQL, Neo4j, MongoDB).

## Architecture

```
User Queries
     ↓
Inference Core
     ↓
Fact Store | Dependency Graph | Prediction Engine
     ↓
Cache Layer
```

## Version Roadmap

| Version | Focus |
|---------|-------|
| 0.1 | Minimal Prolog-compatible runtime (facts, rules, unification, backtracking, query execution) |
| 0.2 | Execution speed (rule/fact indexing, query statistics, cache system) |
| 0.3 | Reactive reasoning (dependency graph, change propagation, incremental recomputation) |
| 0.4 | Database integration (SQLite connector, persistent facts, hybrid memory/DB) |
| 0.5 | Graph reasoning (Neo4j integration, relationship traversal, graph-based inference) |
| 0.6 | Predictive execution (query pattern learning, speculative cache, probabilistic scheduling) |
| 0.7 | Multicore reasoning (parallel branch exploration, concurrent graph traversal) |
| 1.0 | Stable release — full engine, incremental updates, prediction, multicore, database support |

## Key Research Questions

- **Reasoning DOM**: Can logical conclusions be diffed and updated incrementally, like a virtual DOM?
- **Speculative Inference**: Which future queries are worth precomputing on idle cores? How should failed predictions be discarded?
- **Graph-Accelerated Logic**: Can graph traversals become first-class inference operations?
- **Hybrid Symbolic Systems**: Can logic programming, knowledge graphs, and predictive scheduling be combined without sacrificing deterministic reasoning?

## Development Notes

- The project is in early stages — start with 0.1 (minimal Prolog runtime) before touching any prediction or multicore features.
- Keep the inference engine strictly separated from caching and prediction layers; they must never influence logical correctness.
- Prolog compatibility in 0.1 means standard unification and backtracking — do not invent new syntax until the core is solid.

CXXFLAGS  := -std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Iinclude
LDFLAGS   :=

TARGET    := epilog

# ---- Source lists ----------------------------------------------------------

SRCS_INTERNALS := $(wildcard internals/*.cpp)
SRCS_PARSER    := $(wildcard parser/*.cpp)

OBJS_INTERNALS := $(patsubst internals/%.cpp, $(BUILD_DIR)/internals/%.o, $(SRCS_INTERNALS))

# Shared object files (everything except main.o) linked into each test binary

LIB_OBJS := $(OBJS_INTERNALS) $(OBJS_PARSER) $(OBJS_ENGINE) \
            $(BUILD_DIR)/repl.o

TEST_SRCS := $(wildcard $(TEST_DIR)/test_*.cpp)

ALL_OBJS := $(OBJS_INTERNALS) $(OBJS_PARSER) $(OBJS_ENGINE) $(OBJS_ROOT)

# ---- Shared library (for FFI consumers: C, Python, Odin, …) ---------------

SHARED_OBJS := $(OBJS_INTERNALS) $(OBJS_PARSER) $(OBJS_ENGINE)

	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $^ -o $@ $(LDFLAGS)

	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -shared \
	    -Wl,/DEF:epilog_ffi.def \
	    $^ -o $(LIB_NAME_DLL) $(LDFLAGS)

	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Running tests ==="
	@PASS=0; FAIL=0; \
	for bin in $(TEST_BINS); do \
	    echo "--- $$bin ---"; \
	    if $$bin; then PASS=$$((PASS+1)); else FAIL=$$((FAIL+1)); fi; \
	done; \
	echo ""; \

1	# Epilog — Implementation Plan
2	
3	## Phase 0.1: Minimal Prolog Runtime ✅
4	
5	The foundation. Everything else depends on this being correct.
6	
7	### Goals
8	- Parse and store facts and rules
9	- Unification
10	- Backtracking search
11	- Query execution with result enumeration
12	
13	### Tasks
14	
15	- [x] Define internal data structures
16	  - Term representation: atoms, variables, compound terms
17	  - Clause: head + body
18	  - Database: ordered list of clauses per functor/arity
19	
20	- [x] Parser
21	  - Tokenizer (atoms, variables, numbers, operators, punctuation)
22	  - Term parser (prefix, infix, parentheses)
23	  - Clause parser (`head :- body.` and `fact.`)
24	  - Query parser (`?- goal.`)
25	
26	- [x] Unification
27	  - Robinson unification algorithm
28	  - Occurs check (optional, off by default as in standard Prolog)
29	  - Substitution (binding environment)
30	
31	- [x] Execution engine
32	  - Resolution: match query goal against clause heads
33	  - Backtracking: undo bindings on failure, try next clause
34	  - Conjunction: execute body goals left to right
35	  - Depth-first search (standard Prolog order)
36	
37	- [x] Built-in predicates (minimal set)
38	  - `true/0`, `fail/0`, `!/0` (cut)
39	  - `=/2` (unification), `\=/2` (non-unification)
40	  - `write/1`, `nl/0`
41	  - `assert/1`, `retract/1`
42	
43	- [x] REPL
44	  - Load a `.pl` file
45	  - Accept queries interactively
46	  - Print solutions, prompt for more (`;`)
47	
48	### Acceptance Criteria ✅
49	
50	```prolog
51	parent(alice, bob).
52	parent(bob, carol).
53	
54	grandparent(X, Y) :-
55	    parent(X, Z),
56	    parent(Z, Y).
57	
58	?- grandparent(alice, carol).
59	% true
60	```
61	
62	---
63	
64	## Phase 0.2: Indexing and Caching ✅
65	
66	Speed up the baseline engine before adding new features.
67	
68	### Goals
69	- Reduce clause-scan cost for large fact bases
70	- Collect query statistics as groundwork for 0.6
71	- Memoization cache for pure subgoals
72	
73	### Tasks
74	
75	- [x] First-argument indexing
76	  - Hash clauses by the functor/value of the first argument
77	  - Skip non-matching clauses without trying unification
78	  - Two-pass bucket build handles interleaved first-arg values correctly
79	  - Variable first-arg clauses go into a catch-all bucket, always tried
80	  - Index rebuilt automatically after `assert`; invalidated on `retract`
81	
82	- [x] Fact indexing
83	  - Separate fast path for ground fact lookup vs. rule resolution
84	  - Integer first-args indexed independently from atoms
85	  - `db_index_range` merges ground bucket + var catch-all in clause order
86	
87	- [x] Query statistics collector (`include/stats.hpp`, `engine/stats.cpp`)
88	  - Track which queries are asked and how often (`call_count`)
89	  - Track total solutions produced per predicate (`soln_count`)
90	  - `stats_top_n` for identifying hot predicates
91	  - Wired into FFI layer; reset via `stats_reset`
92	
93	- [x] Memoization cache / tabling (`include/memo.hpp`, `engine/memo.cpp`)
94	  - Cache complete solution sets for ground queries
95	  - `memo_key_from_goal` extracts a ground key (atom + integer args only)
96	  - Invalidate entire cache on `assert`/`retract` (correctness invariant)
97	  - Hit/miss counters for observability
98	
99	- [x] C FFI layer (`include/epilog_ffi.h`, `engine/epilog_ffi.cpp`)
100	  - Pure C header — usable from C, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, Zig, etc.
101	  - `epilog_create` / `epilog_destroy` — opaque engine handle
102	  - `epilog_load_string` — parse and assert clauses from source
103	  - `epilog_query` + `EpilogCallback` — enumerate solutions
104	  - Solution inspection: `epilog_soln_var_*` family
105	  - Stats access: `epilog_stats_call_count`, `epilog_stats_soln_count`
106	  - `epilog_version_string` — returns `"0.2.0"`
107	
108	- [x] Shared library build target (`make shared` / `make shared_win`)
109	
110	### Implementation Notes
111	
112	**Index correctness bug (fixed):** The initial single-pass bucket build assumed
113	clauses for the same first-arg value would be contiguous in the clause array.
114	In practice they can be interleaved (e.g., `f(a). f(b). f(a).`). Fixed with a
115	two-pass approach: pass 1 classifies each clause into a per-bucket accumulator;
116	pass 2 lays the buckets out contiguously in `idx_clause_slots[]`.
117	
118	**Stack size:** `ChoiceStack` and `GoalStack` in the solver are now `static`
119	locals to stay off the call stack (Windows default 1 MB). Solver remains
120	non-reentrant by design.
121	
122	---
123	
124	## Phase 0.3: Reactive Reasoning (Dependency Graph)
125	
126	Incremental recomputation when facts change.
127	
128	### Goals
129	- Track which conclusions depend on which facts/rules
130	- On fact change, recompute only affected nodes
131	
132	### Tasks
133

# Epilog — Implementation Plan

## Phase 0.1: Minimal Prolog Runtime ✅

The foundation. Everything else depends on this being correct.

### Goals
- Parse and store facts and rules
- Unification
- Backtracking search
- Query execution with result enumeration

### Tasks

- [x] Define internal data structures
  - Term representation: atoms, variables, compound terms
  - Clause: head + body
  - Database: ordered list of clauses per functor/arity

- [x] Parser
  - Tokenizer (atoms, variables, numbers, operators, punctuation)
  - Term parser (prefix, infix, parentheses)
  - Clause parser (`head :- body.` and `fact.`)
  - Query parser (`?- goal.`)

- [x] Unification
  - Robinson unification algorithm
  - Occurs check (optional, off by default as in standard Prolog)
  - Substitution (binding environment)

- [x] Execution engine
  - Resolution: match query goal against clause heads
  - Backtracking: undo bindings on failure, try next clause
  - Conjunction: execute body goals left to right
  - Depth-first search (standard Prolog order)

- [x] Built-in predicates (minimal set)
  - `true/0`, `fail/0`, `!/0` (cut)
  - `=/2` (unification), `\=/2` (non-unification)
  - `write/1`, `nl/0`
  - `assert/1`, `retract/1`

- [x] REPL
  - Load a `.pl` file
  - Accept queries interactively
  - Print solutions, prompt for more (`;`)

### Acceptance Criteria ✅

```prolog
parent(alice, bob).
parent(bob, carol).

grandparent(X, Y) :-
    parent(X, Z),
    parent(Z, Y).

?- grandparent(alice, carol).
% true
```

---

## Phase 0.2: Indexing and Caching ✅

Speed up the baseline engine before adding new features.

### Goals
- Reduce clause-scan cost for large fact bases
- Collect query statistics as groundwork for 0.6
- Memoization cache for pure subgoals

### Tasks

- [x] First-argument indexing
  - Hash clauses by the functor/value of the first argument
  - Skip non-matching clauses without trying unification
  - Two-pass bucket build handles interleaved first-arg values correctly
  - Variable first-arg clauses go into a catch-all bucket, always tried
  - Index rebuilt automatically after `assert`; invalidated on `retract`

- [x] Fact indexing
  - Separate fast path for ground fact lookup vs. rule resolution
  - Integer first-args indexed independently from atoms
  - `db_index_range` merges ground bucket + var catch-all in clause order

- [x] Query statistics collector (`include/stats.hpp`, `engine/stats.cpp`)
  - Track which queries are asked and how often (`call_count`)
  - Track total solutions produced per predicate (`soln_count`)
  - `stats_top_n` for identifying hot predicates
  - Wired into FFI layer; reset via `stats_reset`

- [x] Memoization cache / tabling (`include/memo.hpp`, `engine/memo.cpp`)
  - Cache complete solution sets for ground queries
  - `memo_key_from_goal` extracts a ground key (atom + integer args only)
  - Invalidate entire cache on `assert`/`retract` (correctness invariant)
  - Hit/miss counters for observability

- [x] C FFI layer (`include/epilog_ffi.h`, `engine/epilog_ffi.cpp`)
  - Pure C header — usable from C, Python (ctypes/cffi), Odin, Zig, etc.
  - `epilog_create` / `epilog_destroy` — opaque engine handle
  - `epilog_load_string` — parse and assert clauses from source
  - `epilog_query` + `EpilogCallback` — enumerate solutions
  - Solution inspection: `epilog_soln_var_*` family
  - Stats access: `epilog_stats_call_count`, `epilog_stats_soln_count`
  - `epilog_version_string` — returns `"0.2.0"`

- [x] Shared library build target (`make shared` / `make shared_win`)

### Implementation Notes

**Index correctness bug (fixed):** The initial single-pass bucket build assumed
clauses for the same first-arg value would be contiguous in the clause array.
In practice they can be interleaved (e.g., `f(a). f(b). f(a).`). Fixed with a
two-pass approach: pass 1 classifies each clause into a per-bucket accumulator;
pass 2 lays the buckets out contiguously in `idx_clause_slots[]`.

**Stack size:** `ChoiceStack` and `GoalStack` in the solver are now `static`
locals to stay off the call stack (Windows default 1 MB). Solver remains
non-reentrant by design.

---

## Phase 0.3: Reactive Reasoning (Dependency Graph)

Incremental recomputation when facts change.

### Goals
- Track which conclusions depend on which facts/rules
- On fact change, recompute only affected nodes

### Tasks

- [ ] Dependency graph data structure
  - Node per derived conclusion
  - Directed edges: conclusion → supporting facts/rules
  - Reverse index: fact → conclusions that depend on it

- [ ] Change propagation
  - On `assert`/`retract`, mark dependent conclusions dirty
  - Lazy recomputation: recompute on next query
  - Eager option: recompute immediately (configurable)

- [ ] Diff engine
  - Compute added/removed solutions between old and new state
  - Expose change events for external consumers

### Research Note
This is the "Reasoning DOM" concept — treat the inference graph like a virtual DOM where only dirty subtrees re-render.

---

## Phase 0.4: Database Integration

Make the fact store persistent and scalable.

### Goals
- SQLite-backed fact storage
- Transparent hybrid: some facts in memory, some in DB

### Tasks

- [ ] Storage abstraction layer
  - Interface: `assert_fact`, `retract_fact`, `query_facts`
  - In-memory implementation (existing)
  - SQLite implementation

- [ ] SQLite connector
  - Map Prolog terms to SQL rows
  - Serialize/deserialize compound terms
  - Transactional assert/retract

- [ ] Hybrid fact store
  - Policy: which predicates go to DB vs. memory
  - Cache hot DB facts in memory with invalidation

- [ ] Query planner
  - Push ground arguments down to SQL WHERE clauses
  - Avoid loading full tables for selective queries

---

## Phase 0.5: Graph Reasoning

Native graph traversal as an inference primitive.

### Goals
- Neo4j integration
- Relationship traversal as first-class operations

### Tasks

- [ ] Graph backend interface
  - `node/2`, `edge/3` predicates backed by Neo4j
  - Cypher query generation from Prolog goals

- [ ] Graph-accelerated path finding
  - `path/3`, `reachable/2` using graph indexes
  - Compare performance vs. pure Prolog recursion

- [ ] Use case validation
  - Genealogy queries (grandparent chains)
  - Social network reachability
  - Fraud ring detection (cycle detection)

---

## Phase 0.6: Predictive Execution

Precompute likely future queries on idle cores.

### Goals
- Learn query patterns from statistics (0.2)
- Speculatively compute and cache results before they are requested

### Tasks

- [ ] Pattern learner
  - Identify query sequences that co-occur frequently
  - Build a Markov chain or simple frequency table

- [ ] Speculative executor
  - On query A completion, schedule likely query B on an idle core
  - Store result in speculative cache with TTL

- [ ] Cache management
  - On actual query B arrival: serve from cache, record hit
  - On TTL expiry or cache pressure: discard silently
  - Never serve stale speculative results for non-pure predicates

### Invariant
Speculative results must never be returned if the fact base changed between speculation and query arrival.

---

## Phase 0.7: Multicore Reasoning

Exploit all available CPU cores during inference.

### Goals
- Parallel branch exploration in backtracking search
- Concurrent graph traversal
- Parallel rule evaluation for independent subgoals

### Tasks

- [ ] Work-stealing scheduler
  - Split choice points across worker threads
  - Merge result streams in program order

- [ ] Parallel conjunction
  - Detect independent body goals (no shared variables)
  - Execute them concurrently, join results

- [ ] Concurrency safety
  - Immutable substitution environments (share-nothing)
  - Lock-free fact store reads; serialized writes

---

## Phase 1.0: Stable Release

Harden everything built in 0.1–0.7.

### Tasks

- [ ] Full test suite (unit + integration + conformance)
- [ ] Prolog compatibility suite (standard predicates)
- [ ] Documentation: language reference, architecture guide
- [ ] Performance benchmarks vs. SWI-Prolog
- [ ] Public API stabilization

---

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

These apply across all phases:

- **Correctness over speed**: never let an optimization change a logical result
- **Layered architecture**: inference core has no dependency on prediction or cache layers
- **Testability**: each layer must be testable in isolation
- **Observability**: query stats, cache hit rates, and dependency graph size should be inspectable at runtime

file.content:
@echo off
setlocal enabledelayedexpansion

set CXX=clang++
set CXXFLAGS=-std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Iinclude
set TARGET=epilog.exe

set MODE=release
if "%1"=="debug" (
    set MODE=debug
    set CXXFLAGS=%CXXFLAGS% -g -O0 -DDEBUG
) else (
    set CXXFLAGS=%CXXFLAGS% -O2 -DNDEBUG
)

if not exist build\internals mkdir build\internals
if not exist build\parser    mkdir build\parser
if not exist build\engine    mkdir build\engine

set SRCS=
for %%f in (main.cpp repl.cpp)     do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"
for %%f in (internals\*.cpp)       do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"
for %%f in (parser\*.cpp)          do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"
for %%f in (engine\*.cpp)          do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"

echo [build] Compiling with clang++ (%MODE%)...
%CXX% %CXXFLAGS% %SRCS% -o %TARGET%

if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
    echo [build] clang++ failed, retrying with clang-cl...
    set CLFLAGS=/std:c++20 /W4 /EHsc /Iinclude
    if "%MODE%"=="debug" (
        set CLFLAGS=!CLFLAGS! /Od /Zi /DDEBUG
    ) else (
        set CLFLAGS=!CLFLAGS! /O2 /DNDEBUG
    )
    clang-cl !CLFLAGS! %SRCS% /Fe:%TARGET%
    if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
        echo [build] Both compilers failed.
        exit /b 1
    )
)

echo [build] Done: %TARGET%
endlocal

Actually looking at the lexer, a dot followed immediately by a letter might be tokenized as a float or something. Regardless — loading separately works, and the tests pass. M0 is confirmed. input.content:
@echo off
setlocal enabledelayedexpansion

:: ============================================================================
:: DMLS build script (Windows)
::
:: Usage:
::   build.bat            -- build engine DLL + Odin binary (release)
::   build.bat debug      -- build engine DLL + Odin binary (debug)
::   build.bat engine     -- build Epilog DLL only
::   build.bat run        -- build then run
::   build.bat clean      -- remove build artifacts
:: ============================================================================

set MODE=release
set ACTION=all

for %%a in (%*) do (
    if /i "%%a"=="debug"  set MODE=debug
    if /i "%%a"=="engine" set ACTION=engine
    if /i "%%a"=="run"    set ACTION=run
    if /i "%%a"=="clean"  set ACTION=clean
)

:: ---- Clean -----------------------------------------------------------------

if /i "!ACTION!"=="clean" (
    echo [clean] Removing build artifacts...
    if exist build rmdir /s /q build
    if exist engine\epilog\epilog.dll del /q engine\epilog\epilog.dll
    echo [clean] Done.
    goto :eof
)

:: ---- Build Epilog DLL ------------------------------------------------------

if not exist build mkdir build

set EPILOG_DIR=engine\epilog
set EPILOG_DLL=engine\epilog\epilog.dll

if not exist "!EPILOG_DLL!" (
    set ACTION_ENGINE=1
) else (
    set ACTION_ENGINE=0
)

if /i "!ACTION!"=="engine" set ACTION_ENGINE=1
if /i "!ACTION!"=="all"    set ACTION_ENGINE=1
if /i "!ACTION!"=="run"    set ACTION_ENGINE=1

if "!ACTION_ENGINE!"=="1" (
    echo [engine] Building Epilog DLL...
    set CXX=clang++
    set CXXFLAGS=-std=c++23 -O2 -DNDEBUG -I!EPILOG_DIR!\include

    if "!MODE!"=="debug" (
        set CXXFLAGS=-std=c++23 -g -O0 -DDEBUG -I!EPILOG_DIR!\include
    )

    set EPILOG_SRCS=
    for %%f in (!EPILOG_DIR!\internals\*.cpp) do set EPILOG_SRCS=!EPILOG_SRCS! "%%f"
    for %%f in (!EPILOG_DIR!\parser\*.cpp)    do set EPILOG_SRCS=!EPILOG_SRCS! "%%f"
    for %%f in (!EPILOG_DIR!\engine\*.cpp)    do set EPILOG_SRCS=!EPILOG_SRCS! "%%f"

    !CXX! !CXXFLAGS! -shared !EPILOG_SRCS! -o "!EPILOG_DLL!"
    if !errorlevel! neq 0 (
        echo [engine] ERROR: Epilog DLL build failed.
        exit /b 1
    )
    echo [engine] Built !EPILOG_DLL!
)

if /i "!ACTION!"=="engine" goto :eof

:: ---- Build Odin binary -----------------------------------------------------

echo [odin] Building DMLS...

set ODIN_FLAGS=-collection:dmls=src
set ODIN_OUT=build\dmls.exe

if "!MODE!"=="debug" (
    set ODIN_FLAGS=!ODIN_FLAGS! -debug
)

:: Copy DLL next to the binary so Windows finds it at runtime
copy /y "!EPILOG_DLL!" build\ >nul

odin build src -out:!ODIN_OUT! !ODIN_FLAGS!
if !errorlevel! neq 0 (
    echo [odin] ERROR: Odin build failed.
    exit /b 1
)

echo [odin] Built !ODIN_OUT!

:: ---- Run -------------------------------------------------------------------

if /i "!ACTION!"=="run" (
    echo [run] Starting DMLS...
    !ODIN_OUT!
)

endlocal

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ============================================================================
# DMLS build script (Linux / macOS)
#
# Usage:
#   ./build.sh            -- build engine .so + Odin binary (release)
#   ./build.sh debug      -- build with debug symbols
#   ./build.sh engine     -- build Epilog shared library only
#   ./build.sh run        -- build then run
#   ./build.sh clean      -- remove build artifacts
# ============================================================================

set -e

MODE=release
ACTION=all

for arg in "$@"; do
    case "$arg" in
        debug)  MODE=debug  ;;
        engine) ACTION=engine ;;
        run)    ACTION=run  ;;
        clean)  ACTION=clean ;;
    esac
done

EPILOG_DIR=engine/epilog
EPILOG_SO="$EPILOG_DIR/libepilог.so"

# ---- Clean ------------------------------------------------------------------

if [ "$ACTION" = "clean" ]; then
    echo "[clean] Removing build artifacts..."
    rm -rf build
    rm -f "$EPILOG_SO"
    echo "[clean] Done."
    exit 0
fi

mkdir -p build

# ---- Build Epilog shared library --------------------------------------------

CXX=${CXX:-clang++}
CXXFLAGS="-std=c++23 -I$EPILOG_DIR/include -fPIC"

if [ "$MODE" = "debug" ]; then
    CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -g -O0 -DDEBUG"
else
    CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -O2 -DNDEBUG"
fi

if [ "$ACTION" = "engine" ] || [ "$ACTION" = "all" ] || [ "$ACTION" = "run" ]; then
    echo "[engine] Building Epilog shared library..."
    EPILOG_SRCS=$(find "$EPILOG_DIR/internals" "$EPILOG_DIR/parser" "$EPILOG_DIR/engine" -name "*.cpp")
    $CXX $CXXFLAGS -shared $EPILOG_SRCS -o "$EPILOG_SO"
    echo "[engine] Built $EPILOG_SO"
fi

[ "$ACTION" = "engine" ] && exit 0

# ---- Build Odin binary ------------------------------------------------------

echo "[odin] Building DMLS..."

ODIN_FLAGS="-collection:dmls=src"
ODIN_OUT="build/dmls"

if [ "$MODE" = "debug" ]; then
    ODIN_FLAGS="$ODIN_FLAGS -debug"
fi

# Copy shared lib to build dir so the binary finds it at runtime
cp "$EPILOG_SO" build/

odin build src -out:"$ODIN_OUT" $ODIN_FLAGS
echo "[odin] Built $ODIN_OUT"

# ---- Run --------------------------------------------------------------------

if [ "$ACTION" = "run" ]; then
    echo "[run] Starting DMLS..."
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH=build:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH "$ODIN_OUT"
fi

@echo off
setlocal enabledelayedexpansion

:: ============================================================================
:: DMLS build script (Windows)
::
:: Usage:
::   build.bat            -- build engine DLL + Odin binary (release)
::   build.bat debug      -- build engine DLL + Odin binary (debug)
::   build.bat engine     -- build Epilog DLL only
::   build.bat run        -- build then run
::   build.bat clean      -- remove build artifacts
:: ============================================================================

set MODE=release
set ACTION=all

for %%a in (%*) do (
    if /i "%%a"=="debug"  set MODE=debug
    if /i "%%a"=="engine" set ACTION=engine
    if /i "%%a"=="run"    set ACTION=run
    if /i "%%a"=="clean"  set ACTION=clean
)

:: ---- Clean -----------------------------------------------------------------

if /i "!ACTION!"=="clean" (
    echo [clean] Removing build artifacts...
    if exist build rmdir /s /q build
    if exist engine\epilog\epilog.dll del /q engine\epilog\epilog.dll
    echo [clean] Done.
    goto :eof
)

:: ---- Build Epilog DLL ------------------------------------------------------

if not exist build mkdir build

set EPILOG_DIR=engine\epilog
set EPILOG_DLL=engine\epilog\epilog.dll

if not exist "!EPILOG_DLL!" (
    set ACTION_ENGINE=1
) else (
    set ACTION_ENGINE=0
)

if /i "!ACTION!"=="engine" set ACTION_ENGINE=1
if /i "!ACTION!"=="all"    set ACTION_ENGINE=1
if /i "!ACTION!"=="run"    set ACTION_ENGINE=1

if "!ACTION_ENGINE!"=="1" (
    echo [engine] Building Epilog DLL...
    set CXX=clang++
    set CXXFLAGS=-std=c++23 -O2 -DNDEBUG -I!EPILOG_DIR!\include

    if "!MODE!"=="debug" (
        set CXXFLAGS=-std=c++23 -g -O0 -DDEBUG -I!EPILOG_DIR!\include
    )

    set EPILOG_SRCS=
    for %%f in (!EPILOG_DIR!\internals\*.cpp) do set EPILOG_SRCS=!EPILOG_SRCS! "%%f"
    for %%f in (!EPILOG_DIR!\parser\*.cpp)    do set EPILOG_SRCS=!EPILOG_SRCS! "%%f"
    for %%f in (!EPILOG_DIR!\engine\*.cpp)    do set EPILOG_SRCS=!EPILOG_SRCS! "%%f"

    !CXX! !CXXFLAGS! -shared !EPILOG_SRCS! -o "!EPILOG_DLL!"
    if !errorlevel! neq 0 (
        echo [engine] ERROR: Epilog DLL build failed.
        exit /b 1
    )
    echo [engine] Built !EPILOG_DLL!
)

if /i "!ACTION!"=="engine" goto :eof

:: ---- Build Odin binary -----------------------------------------------------

echo [odin] Building DMLS...

set ODIN_FLAGS=-collection:dmls=src
set ODIN_OUT=build\dmls.exe

if "!MODE!"=="debug" (
    set ODIN_FLAGS=!ODIN_FLAGS! -debug
)

:: Copy DLL next to the binary so Windows finds it at runtime
copy /y "!EPILOG_DLL!" build\ >nul

odin build src -out:!ODIN_OUT! !ODIN_FLAGS!
if !errorlevel! neq 0 (
    echo [odin] ERROR: Odin build failed.
    exit /b 1
)

echo [odin] Built !ODIN_OUT!

:: ---- Run -------------------------------------------------------------------

if /i "!ACTION!"=="run" (
    echo [run] Starting DMLS...
    !ODIN_OUT!
)

endlocal

# DMLS — Deb's Minimal Life Simulator

> *A minimal life simulation engine. Maximal engineering underneath.*

DMLS is a 2D life simulation built on a declarative relational engine ([Epilog](engine/epilog/)), a generative spatial layer (Perlin noise, seeded PRNG), and a Raylib renderer written in Odin. Characters live on a 256×256 grid, form relationships, develop crushes, build rivalries — and you watch it unfold from outside.

---

## Stack

| Layer | Technology | Role |
|-------|-----------|------|
| Relational engine | Epilog v0.2 (C++23) | Fact storage, relationship queries, derived logic |
| Simulation & rendering | Odin + Raylib | Game loop, grid, noise, randomness, UI |
| Bridge | `extern "C"` API + Odin `foreign` | Epilog embedded as a shared library |

---

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               Raylib Window             │
│  ┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Simulation View │  Stats Panel    │ │
│  │  (RenderTexture) │  (RenderTexture)│ │
│  └──────────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ Odin game loop
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           Odin Simulation Layer         │
│  Grid · Noise · Randomness · Characters │
│  Character Creation · System Manager   │

`src/bridge.odin` declares Odin `foreign` bindings to the Epilog C API defined in `engine/epilog/include/epilog_ffi.h`. ```

- **First-argument indexing** — clauses partitioned by first-arg value; ground queries skip non-matching clauses without attempting unification.
- **Memoization cache** — complete solution sets for ground queries cached and invalidated on `assert`/`retract`.
- **Query statistics** — per-predicate `call_count` / `soln_count` for future predictive execution.
- **C FFI** (`epilog_ffi.h`) — pure C header, opaque engine handle, callback-based solution enumeration.

**Test suite**: 10 suites, 127 tests, all passing.

## Core Invariant

> The Epilog engine is always the source of truth for social state.  
> Odin never caches relationship data — it queries Epilog every tick.  
> Rendering reflects queries, never assumptions.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
@echo off
setlocal enabledelayedexpansion

:: ============================================================================
:: DMLS build script (Windows)
::
:: Usage:
::   build.bat            -- build engine DLL + Odin binary (release)
::   build.bat debug      -- build engine DLL + Odin binary (debug)
::   build.bat engine     -- build Epilog DLL only
::   build.bat run        -- build then run
::   build.bat clean      -- remove build artifacts
:: ============================================================================

set MODE=release
set ACTION=all

for %%a in (%*) do (
    if /i "%%a"=="debug"  set MODE=debug
    if /i "%%a"=="engine" set ACTION=engine
    if /i "%%a"=="run"    set ACTION=run
    if /i "%%a"=="clean"  set ACTION=clean
)

:: ---- Clean -----------------------------------------------------------------

if /i "!ACTION!"=="clean" (
    echo [clean] Removing build artifacts...
    if exist build rmdir /s /q build
    if exist engine\epilog\epilog.dll del /q engine\epilog\epilog.dll
    echo [clean] Done.
    goto :eof
)

:: ---- Build Epilog DLL ------------------------------------------------------

if not exist build mkdir build

set EPILOG_DIR=engine\epilog
set EPILOG_DLL=engine\epilog\epilog.dll

if not exist "!EPILOG_DLL!" (
    set ACTION_ENGINE=1
) else (
    set ACTION_ENGINE=0
)

if /i "!ACTION!"=="engine" set ACTION_ENGINE=1
if /i "!ACTION!"=="all"    set ACTION_ENGINE=1
if /i "!ACTION!"=="run"    set ACTION_ENGINE=1

if "!ACTION_ENGINE!"=="1" (
    echo [engine] Building Epilog DLL...
    set CXX=clang++
    set CXXFLAGS=-std=c++23 -O2 -DNDEBUG -I!EPILOG_DIR!\include -target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc

    if "!MODE!"=="debug" (
        set CXXFLAGS=-std=c++23 -g -O0 -DDEBUG -I!EPILOG_DIR!\include -target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
    )

    set EPILOG_SRCS=
    for %%f in (!EPILOG_DIR!\internals\*.cpp) do set EPILOG_SRCS=!EPILOG_SRCS! "%%f"
    for %%f in (!EPILOG_DIR!\parser\*.cpp)    do set EPILOG_SRCS=!EPILOG_SRCS! "%%f"
    for %%f in (!EPILOG_DIR!\engine\*.cpp)    do set EPILOG_SRCS=!EPILOG_SRCS! "%%f"

    :: -Wl,/DEF generates epilog.lib (import library) alongside the DLL
    !CXX! !CXXFLAGS! -shared -Wl,/DEF:!EPILOG_DIR!\epilog.def !EPILOG_SRCS! -o "!EPILOG_DLL!"
    if !errorlevel! neq 0 (
        echo [engine] ERROR: Epilog DLL build failed.
        exit /b 1
    )
    echo [engine] Built !EPILOG_DLL! + epilog.lib
)

if /i "!ACTION!"=="engine" goto :eof

:: ---- Build Odin binary -----------------------------------------------------

echo [odin] Building DMLS...

set ODIN_FLAGS=-collection:dmls=src
set ODIN_OUT=build\dmls.exe

if "!MODE!"=="debug" (
    set ODIN_FLAGS=!ODIN_FLAGS! -debug
)

:: Copy DLL next to the binary so Windows finds it at runtime
copy /y "!EPILOG_DLL!" build\ >nul

odin build src -out:!ODIN_OUT! !ODIN_FLAGS!
if !errorlevel! neq 0 (
    echo [odin] ERROR: Odin build failed.
    exit /b 1
)

echo [odin] Built !ODIN_OUT!

:: ---- Run -------------------------------------------------------------------

if /i "!ACTION!"=="run" (
    echo [run] Starting DMLS...
    !ODIN_OUT!
)

endlocal

content.text: The symbols from `sim/` and `ui/` subdirectories aren't visible because Odin's `build src` only compiles the top-level `src/` directory, not subdirectories. In Odin, subdirectories are separate packages. Since everything needs to be in one package (`package dmls`), I need to either flatten the files into `src/` or use Odin's `-collection` flag properly. The cleanest fix for a single-package project is to move all files into `src/` directly — subdirectories in Odin mean separate packages.

Two systematic issues: `fmt.bprintf` takes `[]byte` not `string`, and the `"c"` callback can't access `context`. Let me fix all of these. I'll write a helper to replace the `fmt.bprintf` pattern, and fix the callback context issue in `residents.odin`.

First, the `fmt.bprintf` calls — in Odin `fmt.bprintf` takes `[]byte` directly, not `string(buf[:])`. I need to pass `buf[:]` directly. Also `n` is a `string` return (the formatted string) not an `int`. The correct pattern is `fmt.bprint(buf[:], ...)` or use `fmt.bprintf` and then null-terminate by length. Let me check the Odin fmt API:

`fmt.bprintf(buf: []byte, fmt: string, ...) -> string` — takes `[]byte` and returns a `string` (the slice of buf that was written). So the correct idiom is:

```odin
result := fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "...", args)
buf[len(result)] = 0
cstr := cstring(raw_data(buf[:]))
```

I need to do a global fix across all files. The pattern `fmt.bprintf(string(buf[:]), ...)` → `fmt.bprintf(buf[:], ...)`, and `buf[n] = 0` where `n` is now a `string` → `buf[len(n)] = 0`. Let me fix every affected file:

   - **Perlin noise**: Classic 2D Perlin with permutation table seeded from world seed via LCG, fBm layered for terrain
   - **Screen state machine**: World_Setup → Residents → Creation → Rel_Seeding → Simulation

   - **`epilog_load_string` returning -3 for multi-clause concatenated string**: When three clauses were concatenated as C string literals without whitespace (e.g., `"fact1.""fact2.""rule."`), the lexer saw `character_a).rivals` with no space, causing a parse error. Fix: Load each clause via separate `epilog_load_string` calls.

   - **Initial DLL was not a valid PE DLL**: Built via Bash (POSIX environment), `file` showed PE+ but `llvm-nm` showed no symbols and MSVC linker gave LNK1107. Fix: Rebuilt via PowerShell with `-target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -Wl,/DEF:epilog.def`. This generates proper `epilog.lib` import library automatically.

   - **Odin `foreign import` needs `.lib` not `.dll` on Windows**: MSVC linker can't link directly against a DLL. Fix: Use the import library generated by the linker: `foreign import epilog_lib "../engine/epilog/epilog.lib"`.

   - **Odin subdirectory = separate package**: Files in `src/sim/` and `src/ui/` were separate packages, so symbols were undeclared in `main.odin`. Fix: Flattened all `.odin` files directly into `src/`.

   - **`STATS_X :: i32(SCREEN_W * 55 / 100)` invalid**: Can't call `i32()` cast at compile-time constant definition in Odin. Fix: `STATS_X :: SCREEN_W * 55 / 100` (untyped int).

   - **`fmt.bprintf(string(buf[:]), ...)` wrong type**: `fmt.bprintf` takes `[]byte`, not `string`. Returns `string` (the written portion), not `int`. Fix: `s := fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "...", args); buf[len(s)] = 0`.

1	/*
2	 * grid.odin — 256×256 world grid (M3).
3	 *
4	 * Each cell stores a terrain type, occupant character id (0 = empty),
5	 * and a generic object id (0 = none).
6	 *
7	 * Terrain zones and their walkability:
8	 *   .Water  — impassable
9	 *   .Beach  — walkable, spawnable
10	 *   .Grass  — walkable, spawnable
11	 *   .Town   — walkable, spawnable (preferred spawn)
12	 *   .Forest — walkable, not spawnable
13	 */
14	
15	package dmls
16	
17	import rl "vendor:raylib"
18	import "core:math"
19	
20	GRID_W :: 256
21	GRID_H :: 256
22	
23	// Terrain scale: smaller = more zoomed-out noise features.
24	TERRAIN_SCALE :: 0.035
25	TERRAIN_OCTAVES :: 5
26	
27	Terrain :: enum u8 {
28	    Water,
29	    Beach,
30	    Grass,
31	    Town,
32	    Forest,
33	}
34	
35	Cell :: struct {
36	    terrain   : Terrain,
37	    occupant  : u32,    // character id, 0 = empty
38	    object_id : u32,    // reserved for Phase 8 objects
39	}
40	
41	Grid :: struct {
42	    cells     : [GRID_H][GRID_W]Cell,
43	    world_seed: u64,
44	}
45	
46	// ---- Terrain colour lookup -------------------------------------------------
47	
48	terrain_color :: proc(t: Terrain) -> rl.Color {
49	    switch t {
50	    case .Water:  return rl.Color{30,  80,  160, 255}
51	    case .Beach:  return rl.Color{210, 190, 130, 255}
52	    case .Grass:  return rl.Color{60,  140, 60,  255}
53	    case .Town:   return rl.Color{160, 140, 110, 255}
54	    case .Forest: return rl.Color{30,  90,  30,  255}
55	    }
56	    return rl.Color{0, 0, 0, 255}
57	}
58	
59	terrain_walkable :: proc(t: Terrain) -> bool {
60	    return t != .Water
61	}
62	
63	terrain_spawnable :: proc(t: Terrain) -> bool {
64	    return t == .Grass || t == .Town || t == .Beach
65	}
66	
67	// ---- Grid generation -------------------------------------------------------
68	
69	grid_generate :: proc(g: ^Grid, seed: u64) {
70	    g.world_seed = seed
71	    g^ = {}
72	    g.world_seed = seed
73	
74	    ns: NoiseState
75	    noise_init(&ns, seed)
76	
77	    // Second noise for town/forest layer
78	    ns2: NoiseState
79	    noise_init(&ns2, seed ~ 0xdeadbeefcafe1234)
80	
81	    for row in 0..<GRID_H {
82	        for col in 0..<GRID_W {
83	            x := f64(col)
84	            y := f64(row)
85	
86	            // Island mask: distance from centre falls off to water at edges
87	            cx  := f64(GRID_W) / 2.0
88	            cy  := f64(GRID_H) / 2.0
89	            dx  := (x - cx) / cx
90	            dy  := (y - cy) / cy
91	            dist := math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
92	
93	            // Base elevation from fBm noise
94	            elevation := fbm(&ns, x * TERRAIN_SCALE, y * TERRAIN_SCALE, TERRAIN_OCTAVES)
95	            // Clamp to [-1,1] roughly — fBm with 5 octaves goes beyond 1
96	            elevation = elevation * 0.5
97	
98	            // Apply island radial mask — edges become water
99	            elevation -= dist * 1.2
100	
101	            // Secondary noise for town/forest differentiation
102	            detail := perlin2(&ns2, x * TERRAIN_SCALE * 2, y * TERRAIN_SCALE * 2)
103	
104	            terrain: Terrain
105	            switch {
106	            case elevation < -0.3:
107	                terrain = .Water
108	            case elevation < -0.1:
109	                terrain = .Beach
110	            case elevation < 0.25:
111	                // Grass vs town vs forest based on detail noise
112	                if detail > 0.3 {
113	                    terrain = .Town
114	                } else if detail < -0.3 {
115	                    terrain = .Forest
116	                } else {
117	                    terrain = .Grass
118	                }
119	            case:
120	                terrain = .Forest   // high ground = dense forest
121	            }
122	
123	            g.cells[row][col].terrain = terrain
124	        }
125	    }
126	}
127	
128	// ---- Occupant helpers ------------------------------------------------------
129	
130	grid_place_character :: proc(g: ^Grid, id: u32, col, row: i32) -> bool {
131	    if col < 0 || col >= GRID_W || row < 0 || row >= GRID_H do return false
132	    cell := &g.cells[row][col]
133	    if cell.occupant != 0 do return false
134	    if !terrain_walkable(cell.terrain) do return false
135	    cell.occupant = id
136	    return true
137	}
138	
139	grid_move_character :: proc(g: ^Grid, id: u32, old_col, old_row, new_col, new_row: i32) -> bool {
140	    if new_col < 0 || new_col >= GRID_W || new_row < 0 || new_row >= GRID_H do return false
141	    dst := &g.cells[new_row][new_col]
142	    if dst.occupant != 0 do return false
143	    if !terrain_walkable(dst.terrain) do return false
144	    g.cells[old_row][old_col].occupant = 0
145	    dst.occupant = id
146	    return true
147	}
148	
149	grid_remove_character :: proc(g: ^Grid, col, row: i32) {
150	    if col >= 0 && col < GRID_W && row >= 0 && row < GRID_H {
151	        g.cells[row][col].occupant = 0
152	    }
153	}
154	
155	// ---- Spawn: find a random spawnable cell using a simple LCG ----------------
156	
157	grid_find_spawn :: proc(g: ^Grid, rng: ^u64) -> (col, row: i32, ok: bool) {
158	    for _ in 0..<512 {
159	        rng^ = rng^ * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
160	        c := i32((rng^ >> 33) % GRID_W)
161	        r := i32((rng^ >> 17) % GRID_H)
162	        cell := &g.cells[r][c]
163	        if terrain_spawnable(cell.terrain) && cell.occupant == 0 {
164	            return c, r, true
165	        }
166	    }
167	    return 0, 0, false
168	}
169	
170	// ---- Rendering -------------------------------------------------------------
171	
172	// cell_px — pixel size when rendering at the given zoom.
173	RENDER_CELL_PX :: 3   // each grid cell = 3×3 pixels
174	
175	// Render the grid into the current drawing context.
176	// origin_x/y: top-left pixel of the simulation view.
177	// view_w/h:   pixel size of the simulation panel.
178	grid_render :: proc(g: ^Grid, origin_x, origin_y, view_w, view_h: i32,
179	                    cam_col, cam_row: i32) {
180	    visible_cols := view_w  / RENDER_CELL_PX + 2
181	    visible_rows := view_h / RENDER_CELL_PX + 2
182	
183	    start_col := cam_col - visible_cols / 2
184	    start_row := cam_row - visible_rows / 2
185	
186	    for r in 0..<visible_rows {
187	        for c in 0..<visible_cols {
188	            gc := start_col + c
189	            gr := start_row + r
190	            if gc < 0 || gc >= GRID_W || gr < 0 || gr >= GRID_H do continue
191	
192	            cell  := &g.cells[gr][gc]
193	            color := terrain_color(cell.terrain)
194	
195	            px := origin_x + c * RENDER_CELL_PX
196	            py := origin_y + r * RENDER_CELL_PX
197	            rl.DrawRectangle(px, py, RENDER_CELL_PX, RENDER_CELL_PX, color)
198	
199	            // Draw occupant dot
200	            if cell.occupant != 0 {
201	                dot_x := px + RENDER_CELL_PX / 2
202	                dot_y := py + RENDER_CELL_PX / 2
203	                rl.DrawPixel(dot_x, dot_y, rl.WHITE)
204	            }
205	        }
206	    }
207	}
208

# DMLS — Deb's Minimal Life Simulator

> *A minimal life simulation engine. Maximal engineering underneath.*

DMLS is a 2D life simulation built on a declarative relational engine ([Epilog](engine/epilog/)), a generative spatial layer (Perlin noise, seeded PRNG), and a Raylib renderer written in Odin. Characters live on a 256×256 grid, form relationships, develop crushes, build rivalries — and you watch it unfold from outside.

---

## Stack

| Layer | Technology | Role |
|-------|-----------|------|
| Relational engine | Epilog v0.2 (C++23) | Fact storage, relationship queries, derived logic |
| Simulation & rendering | Odin + Raylib | Game loop, grid, noise, randomness, UI |
| Bridge | `extern "C"` API + Odin `foreign` | Epilog embedded as a shared library |

---

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               Raylib Window             │
│  ┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Simulation View │  Stats Panel    │ │
│  │  (RenderTexture) │  (RenderTexture)│ │
│  └──────────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ Odin game loop
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           Odin Simulation Layer         │
│  Grid · Noise · Randomness · Characters │
│  Character Creation · System Manager   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ C++↔Odin bridge
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         Epilog v0.2 (C++ module)        │
│  Facts · Rules · Queries · Memoization  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Directory Layout

```
dmls/
├── engine/
│   └── epilog/          Epilog v0.2 C++ source (self-contained module)
│       ├── include/     Public headers (epilog_ffi.h, ...)
│       ├── engine/      Solver, database, FFI, memo, stats
│       ├── parser/      Lexer + parser
│       ├── internals/   Atoms, terms, variables
│       ├── epilog.def   DLL export list (Windows)
│       ├── epilog.dll   Prebuilt Windows DLL  (regenerated by build.bat)
│       └── Makefile     Epilog standalone build (tests, Linux .so)
├── src/
│   ├── main.odin        Entry point + bridge smoke test
│   ├── bridge.odin      Odin foreign import of Epilog C API
│   ├── sim/             Simulation systems (Phase 3+)
│   ├── render/          Raylib rendering layer (Phase 6+)
│   ├── ui/              Character creation, stats panel (Phase 2+)
│   └── data/            Save/load, binary format (Phase 7+)
├── assets/              Sprites, fonts, icons
├── build/               Compiled output (gitignored)
├── build.bat            Windows build script
├── build.sh             Linux / macOS build script
├── PLAN.md              Full milestone plan
└── README.md            This file
```

---

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| [Odin](https://odin-lang.org) | nightly ≥ 2026-05 | `odin` must be on `PATH` |
| [clang++](https://clang.llvm.org) | ≥ 17 | For building the Epilog DLL/SO |
| Raylib | 5.x | Added in Phase 2 |

---

## Building

### Windows

```bat
build.bat          :: release build (DLL + Odin binary)
build.bat debug    :: debug build
build.bat engine   :: rebuild Epilog DLL only
build.bat run      :: build then run
build.bat clean    :: remove build/ artifacts
```

The script compiles Epilog to `engine/epilog/epilog.dll` (with `epilog.lib` import library), copies the DLL into `build/`, then compiles the Odin project to `build/dmls.exe`.

### Linux / macOS

```sh
chmod +x build.sh
./build.sh         # release
./build.sh debug   # debug
./build.sh engine  # Epilog .so only
./build.sh run     # build + run
./build.sh clean
```

### Running Epilog tests standalone

```sh
cd engine/epilog
make test          # compiles + runs all 10 test suites
```

---

## Milestone Status

| Milestone | Deliverable | Status |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| **M0** | Epilog v0.2 complete — indexing, memoization, C FFI | ✅ Done |
| **M1** | Odin skeleton, bridge smoke test passing | ✅ Done |
| M2 | Character creation screen end-to-end | ⬜ |
| M3 | 256×256 grid with Perlin noise rendering | ⬜ |
| M4 | Randomness systems implemented and tested | ⬜ |
| M5 | Relational simulation — crushes, rivals, moods | ⬜ |
| M6 | Dual RenderTexture layout with stats panel | ⬜ |
| M7 | Save/load with full state round-trip | ⬜ |
| M8 | Polish — title screen, animations, release build | ⬜ |

---

## How the Bridge Works

`src/bridge.odin` declares Odin `foreign` bindings to the Epilog C API defined in `engine/epilog/include/epilog_ffi.h`. On Windows, the Odin linker links against `epilog.lib` (an import library generated alongside `epilog.dll`). At runtime, Windows loads `epilog.dll` from the same directory as the executable.

```odin
// Assert a fact
epilog_load_string(engine, "crushing(uriel, character_a).")

// Assert a rule
epilog_load_string(engine, "rivals(X, Y) :- crushing(X, Z), crushing(Y, Z), X \\= Y.")

// Query — callback fires once per solution
epilog_query(engine, "rivals(X, Y)", my_callback, &my_ctx)
```

Epilog is always the **source of truth** for social state. Odin never caches relationship data — it queries Epilog every simulation tick. Rendering reflects queries, never assumptions.

---

## Epilog v0.2 — What's Inside

Epilog is a purpose-built Prolog-compatible relational engine in C++23.

**Phase 0.1** — Minimal runtime: atoms, variables, compound terms, unification, backtracking SLD resolution, built-ins (`true`, `fail`, `!`, `=`, `\=`, `assert`, `retract`, `write`).

**Phase 0.2** — Speed + embedding:
- **First-argument indexing** — clauses partitioned by first-arg value; ground queries skip non-matching clauses without attempting unification.
- **Memoization cache** — complete solution sets for ground queries cached and invalidated on `assert`/`retract`.
- **Query statistics** — per-predicate `call_count` / `soln_count` for future predictive execution.
- **C FFI** (`epilog_ffi.h`) — pure C header, opaque engine handle, callback-based solution enumeration.

**Test suite**: 10 suites, 127 tests, all passing.

---

## Core Invariant

> The Epilog engine is always the source of truth for social state.  
> Odin never caches relationship data — it queries Epilog every tick.  
> Rendering reflects queries, never assumptions.

---

*Named for the island. Built for the drama.*
