# DMLS — Deb's Minimal Life Simulator

> *A minimal life simulation engine. Maximal engineering underneath.*

DMLS is a 2D life simulation built on a declarative relational engine (Epilog), a generative spatial layer (Perlin noise, seeded PRNG), and a Raylib renderer written in Odin. Characters live on a 256×256 grid, form relationships, develop crushes, build rivalries — and you watch it unfold from outside.

---

## Stack

| Layer | Technology | Role |
|-------|-----------|------|
| Relational engine | Epilog v0.2 (C++23) | Fact storage, relationship queries, derived logic |
| Simulation & rendering | Odin + Raylib | Game loop, grid, noise, randomness, UI |
| Bridge | `extern "C"` API + Odin `foreign` | Epilog embedded as a C++ module |

---

## Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               Raylib Window             │
│  ┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Simulation View │  Stats Panel    │ │
│  │  (RenderTexture) │  (RenderTexture)│ │
│  └──────────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ Odin game loop
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           Odin Simulation Layer         │
│  Grid · Noise · Randomness · Characters │
│  Character Creation · System Manager   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ C++↔Odin bridge
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         Epilog v0.2 (C++ module)        │
│  Facts · Rules · Queries · Memoization  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Phase 0: Epilog v0.2 (Prerequisite)

Complete the relational engine before DMLS begins.

### Tasks

- [ ] First-argument indexing
  - Hash clauses by functor/value of first argument
  - Skip non-matching clauses without attempting unification
  - Fast path for ground fact lookup vs rule resolution

- [ ] Memoization cache
  - Cache results of pure (side-effect-free) subgoals
  - Invalidate on `assert`/`retract`
  - Do not cache predicates with side effects (`write`, `nl`)

- [ ] Embedding API (`extern "C"`)
  - `epilog_init()` — initialise all arenas and tables
  - `epilog_assert(fact: *c_char)` — assert a fact string
  - `epilog_retract(fact: *c_char)` — retract a matching fact
  - `epilog_query_bool(goal: *c_char) -> bool` — yes/no query
  - `epilog_query_bindings(goal: *c_char) -> EpilogResult*` — return variable bindings
  - `epilog_free_result(result: EpilogResult*)` — release result memory
  - `epilog_shutdown()` — tear down cleanly

- [ ] Copy source to `dmls/engine/epilog/` as self-contained module

### Acceptance Criteria

```prolog
crushing(uriel, character_a).
crushing(anna_croft, character_a).
rivals(X, Y) :- crushing(X, Z), crushing(Y, Z), X \= Y.
?- rivals(uriel, anna_croft).   % true
?- rivals(X, character_a).        % fail — character_a has no crush
```

---

## Phase 1: Project Skeleton

Stand up the Odin project and confirm the bridge works end-to-end.

### Tasks

- [ ] Directory structure

```
dmls/
├── engine/
│   └── epilog/          Epilog v0.2 C++ source (copied module)
├── src/
│   ├── main.odin        Entry point
│   ├── bridge.odin      foreign import of Epilog C API
│   ├── sim/             Simulation systems
│   ├── render/          Raylib rendering layer
│   ├── ui/              Character creation, stats panel
│   └── data/            Save/load, binary format
├── assets/              Sprites, fonts, icons
├── build.sh / build.bat
└── DMLS_PLAN.md
```

- [ ] Build system
  - Compile Epilog to `epilog.a` / `epilog.lib`
  - Odin build links against it via `foreign import`
  - Single build script for Linux and Windows

- [ ] Bridge smoke test
  - Assert a fact from Odin, query it back, confirm result
  - Confirm `epilog_query_bindings` returns correct variable values

---

## Phase 2: Character Creation Screen

Characters must exist before the simulation means anything.

### Character Data

```odin
Character :: struct {
    id          : u32,
    name        : string,
    nickname    : string,         // what others call them
    age         : u8,
    gender      : Gender,
    dating_pref : DatingPref,
    personality : Personality,    // e.g. Ambitious_Achiever
    pronouns    : Pronouns,
    position    : [2]i32,         // grid cell
    sprite      : u32,            // sprite index
}
```

### Tasks

- [ ] Character creation UI
  - Name and nickname input fields
  - Age, gender, dating preference selectors
  - Personality type picker (Ambitious, Outgoing, etc.)
  - Pronoun selector
  - Sprite selector (palette-swappable base sprites)
  - Confirm screen — "Does everything look good?"

- [ ] Relationship seeding screen
  - After creating a character, optionally tag existing residents
  - Tags: Friend, Sibling, Stranger, Partner (pre-seeds Epilog facts)

- [ ] Assert character into Epilog on creation
  - `character(id, name, personality)`
  - `dating_pref(id, male)` / `dating_pref(id, female)` / `dating_pref(id, any)`
  - `relationship(id_a, id_b, friend)` etc.

- [ ] Resident list screen
  - View all current island residents
  - Select to inspect relationship graph

---

## Phase 3: Grid and World

The spatial layer the simulation lives on.

### Tasks

- [ ] 256×256 grid
  - Each cell stores: terrain type, occupant ID (or empty), object ID
  - Grid rendered as the simulation view (left RenderTexture)

- [ ] Perlin noise terrain generation
  - Implement or port a minimal Perlin noise generator in Odin
  - Generate terrain at world creation: beach, grass, town, forest zones
  - Seed-reproducible — same seed = same island

- [ ] World seed system
  - World seed stored in save file header
  - Displayed on stats panel
  - Can be entered manually at world creation

- [ ] Character placement
  - Spawn characters at valid grid positions (town/grass zones)
  - Characters wander autonomously each tick within their zone

---

## Phase 4: Randomness Systems

Two independent randomness axes — spatial/generative and social/event-driven.

### Independent Randomness
Pure draws with no memory. Used for: terrain events, item drops, idle animations.

```odin
independent_rand :: proc(seed: u64) -> f64 { ... }
```

### Dependent Randomness
Seeded chains where one outcome influences the next. Used for: relationship progression, mood shifts, crush development.

```odin
DependentRNG :: struct {
    state : u64,
    seq   : u64,
}

dependent_next :: proc(rng: ^DependentRNG) -> f64 { ... }
```

### Weighted Randomness
Draw from a distribution. Used for: personality assignment, event selection.

```odin
weighted_choice :: proc(options: []string, weights: []f64) -> string { ... }
```

### Non-weighted Randomness
Uniform draw from a set. Used for: idle dialogue, sprite variation.

### Tasks

- [ ] Implement all four randomness modes in `src/sim/rand.odin`
- [ ] Expose seed state for save/load
- [ ] Confirm dependent RNG produces identical sequences from same seed

---

## Phase 5: Relational Simulation

The Epilog-powered social layer.

### Relationship Facts

```prolog
character(deb, ambitious_achiever).
character(uriel, outgoing_merrymaker).
character(anna, outgoing_dynamo).

crushing(uriel, deb).
friend(deb, uriel).
acquaintance(anna, deb).
stranger(anna, uriel).
sibling(saloni, deb).
```

### Derived Rules

```prolog
rivals(X, Y) :-
    crushing(X, Z),
    crushing(Y, Z),
    X \= Y.

eligible(X, Y) :-
    dating_pref(X, Pref),
    gender(Y, Pref),
    \+ partner(X, _),
    \+ sibling(X, Y).

best_friends(X, Y) :-
    friend(X, Y),
    friend(Y, X),
    interaction_count(X, Y, N),
    N > 10.
```

### Tasks

- [ ] Define base fact schema (character, relationship, interaction_count, mood)
- [ ] Write derived rules for: rivals, eligible, best_friends, unrequited
- [ ] Tick system — every N real seconds = 1 simulation tick
  - Characters near each other increment `interaction_count`
  - Dependent RNG decides if a crush develops this tick
  - Query `eligible(X, Y)` before allowing crush to form
  - Assert new crush facts, retract stale ones

- [ ] Crush resolution
  - If a character develops two crushes, surface a player prompt
  - Player chooses — losing crush relationship unchanged
  - Reflects the Tomodachi Life mechanic accurately

- [ ] Mood system
  - Each character has a mood: happy, content, sad, lovestruck, jealous
  - Derived from relationship state each tick
  - `mood(X, jealous) :- rivals(X, _).`

---

## Phase 6: Rendering

Two RenderTextures composited onto a single Raylib window.

### Layout

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  DMLS — Yggdrasilz                        [seed: ...]│
├─────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┤
│                             │  ISLAND STATS          │
│     Simulation View         │  Residents: 4          │
│     (256×256 grid)          │  Active crushes: 2     │
│                             │  Rival pairs: 1        │
│                             │  Tick: 00:04:32        │
│                             │─────────────────────── │
│                             │  RELATIONSHIPS         │
│                             │  uriel → deb [crush]   │
│                             │  anna ↔ deb [acquaint] │
│                             │  deb ↔ saloni [sibling]│
│                             │─────────────────────── │
│                             │  EVENTS                │
│                             │  [04:31] uriel stares  │
│                             │  [04:28] anna & deb    │
│                             │  trade stories         │
└─────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘
```

### Tasks

- [ ] Two `RenderTexture2D` — simulation and stats panel
- [ ] Simulation view: grid tiles, character sprites, relationship arrows on hover
- [ ] Stats panel: resident list, active crushes, rival pairs, event log, tick counter
- [ ] Event log — rolling last 10 social events (crush formed, rivals detected, mood change)
- [ ] Hover inspect — click a character to see their full relationship list
- [ ] Update rates: simulation at 60fps, stats panel at 10fps

---

## Phase 7: Save and Load

### Binary Save Format

```
[4 bytes]  Magic: "DMLS"
[4 bytes]  Version: u32
[8 bytes]  World seed: u64
[4 bytes]  Tick count: u32
[4 bytes]  Character count: u32
[N bytes]  Character records (fixed-size structs)
[4 bytes]  Fact count: u32
[N bytes]  Epilog fact strings (length-prefixed)
[4 bytes]  Event log entry count: u32
[N bytes]  Event log entries (length-prefixed strings)
[4 bytes]  Checksum: CRC32
```

### Tasks

- [ ] Serialise grid state to binary
- [ ] Serialise all current Epilog facts as strings (via `write/1` dump)
- [ ] Serialise dependent RNG state (seed + sequence counter)
- [ ] Deserialise on load — re-assert all facts into fresh Epilog instance
- [ ] CRC32 checksum validation on load
- [ ] Auto-save every 60 ticks

---

## Phase 8: Polish

- [ ] Title screen with world name input and seed entry
- [ ] Island naming screen ("Yggdrasilz")
- [ ] Relationship event cutscenes (simple sprite animation overlay)
- [ ] Idle animations per personality type
- [ ] Sound effects via Raylib audio (optional)
- [ ] README and build instructions

---

## Milestones

| Milestone | Deliverable |
|-----------|-------------|
| M0 | Epilog v0.2 complete, embedding API working |
| M1 | Odin skeleton, bridge smoke test passing |
| M2 | Character creation screen end-to-end |

| M6 | Dual RenderTexture layout with stats panel |
| M7 | Save/load working with full state round-trip |
| M8 | Polish pass — title screen, animations, release build |

---

## Core Invariant

> The Epilog engine is always the source of truth for social state.
> Odin never caches relationship data — it queries Epilog every tick.
> Rendering reflects queries, never assumptions.

---

50	    return string(f.buf[:f.len])

1	/*
2	 * noise.odin — Seed-reproducible Perlin noise (M3).
3	 *
4	 * Classic permutation-table Perlin noise (Ken Perlin, 2002 improved version).
5	 * The permutation table is derived from the world seed so the same seed always
6	 * produces the same island.
7	 */
8	
9	package dmls
10	
11	import "core:math"
12	
13	// ---- Permutation table -----------------------------------------------------
14	
15	PERM_SIZE :: 256
16	
17	NoiseState :: struct {
18	    perm : [PERM_SIZE * 2]u8,   // doubled for fast wrapping
19	}
20	
21	noise_init :: proc(ns: ^NoiseState, seed: u64) {
22	    // Fill 0..255 then shuffle via LCG seeded by world seed.
23	    for i in 0..<PERM_SIZE {
24	        ns.perm[i] = u8(i)
25	    }
26	    s := seed
27	    for i := PERM_SIZE - 1; i > 0; i -= 1 {
28	        s = s * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
29	        j := int((s >> 33) % u64(i + 1))
30	        ns.perm[i], ns.perm[j] = ns.perm[j], ns.perm[i]
31	    }
32	    for i in 0..<PERM_SIZE {
33	        ns.perm[i + PERM_SIZE] = ns.perm[i]
34	    }
35	}
36	
37	// ---- Gradient function (Perlin 2002) ---------------------------------------
38	
39	_fade :: proc(t: f64) -> f64 {
40	    return t * t * t * (t * (t * 6 - 15) + 10)
41	}
42	
43	_lerp :: proc(a, b, t: f64) -> f64 {
44	    return a + t * (b - a)
45	}
46	
47	_grad :: proc(hash: u8, x, y: f64) -> f64 {
48	    switch hash & 7 {
49	    case 0: return  x + y
50	    case 1: return -x + y
51	    case 2: return  x - y
52	    case 3: return -x - y
53	    case 4: return  x
54	    case 5: return -x
55	    case 6: return  y
56	    case 7: return -y
57	    }
58	    return 0
59	}
60	
61	// perlin2 returns a value in [-1, 1].
62	perlin2 :: proc(ns: ^NoiseState, x, y: f64) -> f64 {
63	    xi := int(math.floor(x)) & 255
64	    yi := int(math.floor(y)) & 255
65	
66	    xf := x - math.floor(x)
67	    yf := y - math.floor(y)
68	
69	    u := _fade(xf)
70	    v := _fade(yf)
71	
72	    aa := int(ns.perm[ns.perm[xi  ] + u8(yi  )])
73	    ab := int(ns.perm[ns.perm[xi  ] + u8(yi+1)])
74	    ba := int(ns.perm[ns.perm[xi+1] + u8(yi  )])
75	    bb := int(ns.perm[ns.perm[xi+1] + u8(yi+1)])
76	
77	    x1 := _lerp(_grad(u8(aa), xf,   yf  ),
78	                 _grad(u8(ba), xf-1, yf  ), u)
79	    x2 := _lerp(_grad(u8(ab), xf,   yf-1),
80	                 _grad(u8(bb), xf-1, yf-1), u)
81	    return _lerp(x1, x2, v)
82	}
83	
84	// fbm — fractional Brownian motion: sum of `octaves` layers.
85	fbm :: proc(ns: ^NoiseState, x, y: f64, octaves: int) -> f64 {
86	    val, amp, freq := 0.0, 1.0, 1.0
87	    for _ in 0..<octaves {
88	        val  += perlin2(ns, x * freq, y * freq) * amp
89	        amp  *= 0.5
90	        freq *= 2.0
91	    }
92	    return val
93	}

# DMLS — Deb's Minimal Life Simulator

> *A minimal life simulation engine. Maximal engineering underneath.*

DMLS is a 2D life simulation built on a declarative relational engine ([Epilog](engine/epilog/)), a generative spatial layer (Perlin noise, seeded PRNG), and a Raylib renderer written in Odin. Characters live on a 256×256 grid, form relationships, develop crushes, build rivalries — and you watch it unfold from outside.

---

## Stack

| Layer | Technology | Role |
|-------|-----------|------|
| Relational engine | Epilog v0.2 (C++23) | Fact storage, relationship queries, derived logic |
| Simulation & rendering | Odin + Raylib | Game loop, grid, noise, randomness, UI |
| Bridge | `extern "C"` API + Odin `foreign` | Epilog embedded as a shared library |

---

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               Raylib Window             │
│  ┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Simulation View │  Stats Panel    │ │
│  │  (RenderTexture) │  (RenderTexture)│ │
│  └──────────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ Odin game loop
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           Odin Simulation Layer         │
│  Grid · Noise · Randomness · Characters │
│  Character Creation · System Manager   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ C++↔Odin bridge
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         Epilog v0.2 (C++ module)        │
│  Facts · Rules · Queries · Memoization  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Directory Layout

```
dmls/
├── engine/
│   └── epilog/          Epilog v0.2 C++ source (self-contained module)
│       ├── include/     Public headers (epilog_ffi.h, ...)
│       ├── engine/      Solver, database, FFI, memo, stats
│       ├── parser/      Lexer + parser
│       ├── internals/   Atoms, terms, variables
│       ├── epilog.def   DLL export list (Windows)
│       ├── epilog.dll   Prebuilt Windows DLL  (regenerated by build.bat)
│       └── Makefile     Epilog standalone build (tests, Linux .so)
├── src/
│   ├── main.odin        Entry point + bridge smoke test
│   ├── bridge.odin      Odin foreign import of Epilog C API
│   ├── sim/             Simulation systems (Phase 3+)
│   ├── render/          Raylib rendering layer (Phase 6+)
│   ├── ui/              Character creation, stats panel (Phase 2+)
│   └── data/            Save/load, binary format (Phase 7+)
├── assets/              Sprites, fonts, icons
├── build/               Compiled output (gitignored)
├── build.bat            Windows build script
├── build.sh             Linux / macOS build script
├── PLAN.md              Full milestone plan
└── README.md            This file
```

---

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| [Odin](https://odin-lang.org) | nightly ≥ 2026-05 | `odin` must be on `PATH` |
| [clang++](https://clang.llvm.org) | ≥ 17 | For building the Epilog DLL/SO |
| Raylib | 5.x | Added in Phase 2 |

---

## Building

### Windows

```bat
build.bat          :: release build (DLL + Odin binary)
build.bat debug    :: debug build
build.bat engine   :: rebuild Epilog DLL only
build.bat run      :: build then run
build.bat clean    :: remove build/ artifacts
```

The script compiles Epilog to `engine/epilog/epilog.dll` (with `epilog.lib` import library), copies the DLL into `build/`, then compiles the Odin project to `build/dmls.exe`.

### Linux / macOS

```sh
chmod +x build.sh
./build.sh         # release
./build.sh debug   # debug
./build.sh engine  # Epilog .so only
./build.sh run     # build + run
./build.sh clean
```

### Running Epilog tests standalone

```sh
cd engine/epilog
make test          # compiles + runs all 10 test suites
```

---

## Milestone Status

| Milestone | Deliverable | Status |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| **M0** | Epilog v0.2 complete — indexing, memoization, C FFI | ✅ Done |
| **M1** | Odin skeleton, bridge smoke test passing | ✅ Done |
| **M2** | Character creation screen end-to-end | ✅ Done |
| **M3** | 256×256 grid with Perlin noise rendering | ✅ Done |
| M4 | Randomness systems implemented and tested | ⬜ |
| M5 | Relational simulation — crushes, rivals, moods | ⬜ |
| M6 | Dual RenderTexture layout with stats panel | ⬜ |
| M7 | Save/load with full state round-trip | ⬜ |
| M8 | Polish — title screen, animations, release build | ⬜ |

---

## How the Bridge Works

`src/bridge.odin` declares Odin `foreign` bindings to the Epilog C API defined in `engine/epilog/include/epilog_ffi.h`. On Windows, the Odin linker links against `epilog.lib` (an import library generated alongside `epilog.dll`). At runtime, Windows loads `epilog.dll` from the same directory as the executable.

```odin
// Assert a fact
epilog_load_string(engine, "crushing(uriel, character_a).")

// Assert a rule
epilog_load_string(engine, "rivals(X, Y) :- crushing(X, Z), crushing(Y, Z), X \\= Y.")

// Query — callback fires once per solution
epilog_query(engine, "rivals(X, Y)", my_callback, &my_ctx)
```

Epilog is always the **source of truth** for social state. Odin never caches relationship data — it queries Epilog every simulation tick. Rendering reflects queries, never assumptions.

---

## Epilog v0.2 — What's Inside

Epilog is a purpose-built Prolog-compatible relational engine in C++23.

**Phase 0.1** — Minimal runtime: atoms, variables, compound terms, unification, backtracking SLD resolution, built-ins (`true`, `fail`, `!`, `=`, `\=`, `assert`, `retract`, `write`).

**Phase 0.2** — Speed + embedding:
- **First-argument indexing** — clauses partitioned by first-arg value; ground queries skip non-matching clauses without attempting unification.
- **Memoization cache** — complete solution sets for ground queries cached and invalidated on `assert`/`retract`.
- **Query statistics** — per-predicate `call_count` / `soln_count` for future predictive execution.
- **C FFI** (`epilog_ffi.h`) — pure C header, opaque engine handle, callback-based solution enumeration.

**Test suite**: 10 suites, 127 tests, all passing.

---

## Core Invariant

> The Epilog engine is always the source of truth for social state.  
> Odin never caches relationship data — it queries Epilog every tick.  
> Rendering reflects queries, never assumptions.

---

*Named for the island. Built for the drama.*

M4–M6 are done. Here's what was built:

**M4 — `rand.odin`**
- `independent_rand` — stateless Splitmix64 hash, no state needed
- `DependentRNG` / `dependent_next` — PCG-style chain; same seed → same sequence
- `weighted_choice_f64` / `weighted_choice_int` — draw from a distribution
- `uniform_choice` — uniform index pick

**M5 — `sim.odin`**
- `SimState` with `DependentRNG`, per-character `CharSocial` (mood + interaction count + crush flag), and a ring-buffer `EventLog`
- `sim_tick` runs every second: proximity detection → interaction count assertion → crush development (0.3% chance per proximity tick, gated by `eligible(X,Y)` Epilog query) → mood re-derivation (`jealous` → `lovestruck` → `happy` → `content`)
- Additional Epilog rules: `mood/2`, `unrequited/2`

**M6 — dual `RenderTexture2D` in `main.odin`**
- `sim_tex` (55% width) redrawn at 60fps: grid, coloured character dots, WASD pan, hover name/mood tooltip, relationship arrows on hover (yellow lines to all linked characters)
- `stat_tex` (45% width) redrawn at 10fps: island stats header, residents with mood badges, rolling event log (last 8 events), navigate button
- Both textures composited with `DrawTexturePro` (Y-flip for RenderTexture convention)

407	// ---- Stats panel click handling (on composited window coords) -------------
408	
409	_handle_stat_clicks :: proc(app: ^App) {
410	    // "Residents ->" button is drawn at (UI_PAD, y) in stat_tex coords.
411	    // In window coords it starts at STATS_X + UI_PAD.
412	    // We re-derive the y based on fixed layout metrics.
413	    res_rows    := i32(app.residents.count)
414	    res_empty   := app.residents.count == 0 ? i32(18) : i32(0)
415	    evt_shown   := i32(min(app.sim.log.count, 8))
416	    evt_empty   := app.sim.log.count == 0 ? i32(18) : i32(0)
417	    base_y := i32(UI_PAD) +
418	        i32(24 + 20 + 18*4 + 8) +
419	        i32(10 + 20) + 18 * res_rows + res_empty + i32(8) +
420	        i32(10 + 10 + 20) +
421	        18 * evt_shown + evt_empty + i32(8) +
422	        i32(10 + 10 + 20)
423	
424	    wx  := i32(STATS_X) + UI_PAD
425	    wy  := base_y
426	    res_rect := rl.Rectangle{f32(wx), f32(wy), 160, 30}
427	    if rl.CheckCollisionPointRec(rl.GetMousePosition(), res_rect) &&
428	       rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.LEFT) {
429	        app.screen = .Residents
430	        app.resident_list = {}
431	    }

434	// ---- Simulation update + composite ----------------------------------------
435	
436	_update_simulation :: proc(app: ^App) {
437	    dt := rl.GetFrameTime()
438	
439	    // WASD camera pan
440	    if rl.IsKeyDown(.W) { app.cam_row -= 2 }
441	    if rl.IsKeyDown(.S) { app.cam_row += 2 }
442	    if rl.IsKeyDown(.A) { app.cam_col -= 2 }
443	    if rl.IsKeyDown(.D) { app.cam_col += 2 }
444	    app.cam_col = clamp(app.cam_col, 0, GRID_W - 1)
445	    app.cam_row = clamp(app.cam_row, 0, GRID_H - 1)
446	
447	    // Simulation tick at ~1 Hz (wander + social sim)
448	    app.sim_timer += dt
449	    if app.sim_timer >= 1.0 {
450	        app.sim_timer = 0
451	        world_tick_wander(&app.world, &app.residents)
452	        sim_tick(&app.sim, &app.residents, app.engine, app.world.tick)
453	    }
454	
455	    // Redraw sim view every frame (60 fps)
456	    _draw_sim_view(app)
457	
458	    // Redraw stats panel at 10 fps
459	    app.stat_timer += dt
460	    if app.stat_timer >= STAT_RATE {
461	        app.stat_timer = 0
462	        _draw_stat_panel(app)
463	    }
464	
465	    // Composite both textures onto the window
466	    rl.ClearBackground(rl.BLACK)
467	
468	    // sim_tex: origin (0, 0), drawn normal
469	    src_sim := rl.Rectangle{0, 0, f32(SIM_W), -f32(SIM_H)}   // flip Y (RenderTexture is upside-down)
470	    dst_sim := rl.Rectangle{0, 0, f32(SIM_W), f32(SIM_H)}
471	    rl.DrawTexturePro(app.sim_tex.texture, src_sim, dst_sim, {0, 0}, 0, rl.WHITE)
472	
473	    // stat_tex: origin (STATS_X, 0)
474	    src_stat := rl.Rectangle{0, 0, f32(STAT_W), -f32(STAT_H)}
475	    dst_stat := rl.Rectangle{f32(STATS_X), 0, f32(STAT_W), f32(STAT_H)}
476	    rl.DrawTexturePro(app.stat_tex.texture, src_stat, dst_stat, {0, 0}, 0, rl.WHITE)
477	
478	    // Divider line
479	    rl.DrawLine(i32(STATS_X), 0, i32(STATS_X), i32(SCREEN_H), COL_MUTED)
480	
481	    // Handle stat panel button clicks (in window space)
482	    _handle_stat_clicks(app)
483	}

487	main :: proc() {
488	    rl.SetConfigFlags({.WINDOW_RESIZABLE})
489	    rl.InitWindow(SCREEN_W, SCREEN_H, "DMLS — Deb's Minimal Life Simulator")
490	    rl.SetTargetFPS(60)
491	    defer rl.CloseWindow()
492	
493	    app := new(App)
494	    defer free(app)
495	    app.engine = epilog_create()
496	    defer epilog_destroy(app.engine)
497	
498	    residents_init(&app.residents)
499	    app.screen  = .World_Setup
500	    app.cam_col = GRID_W / 2
501	    app.cam_row = GRID_H / 2
502	
503	    // Seed entry: show default seed
504	    {
505	        def := _default_seed()
506	        ds  := fmt.bprintf(app.seed_field.buf[:], "%016X", def)
507	        app.seed_field.len = len(ds)
508	        app.seed_field.active = true
509	    }
510	
511	    // Load all Epilog rules (M1 base rules + M5 derived rules)
512	    epilog_load_string(app.engine,
513	        "rivals(X, Y) :- crushing(X, Z), crushing(Y, Z), X \\= Y.")
514	    epilog_load_string(app.engine,
515	        "eligible(X, Y) :- dating_pref(X, Pref), gender(Y, Pref), X \\= Y.")
516	    epilog_load_string(app.engine,
517	        "best_friends(X, Y) :- relationship(X, Y, friend), relationship(Y, X, friend).")
518	    sim_load_rules(app.engine)
519	
520	    // Create RenderTextures for M6 dual-panel layout
521	    app.sim_tex  = rl.LoadRenderTexture(SIM_W, SIM_H)
522	    app.stat_tex = rl.LoadRenderTexture(STAT_W, STAT_H)
523	    app.rt_ready = true
524	    defer rl.UnloadRenderTexture(app.sim_tex)
525	    defer rl.UnloadRenderTexture(app.stat_tex)
526	
527	    for !rl.WindowShouldClose() {
528	        rl.BeginDrawing()
529	        free_all(context.temp_allocator)
530	
531	        switch app.screen {
532	
533	        case .World_Setup:
534	            if _draw_world_setup(app) {
535	                world_seed := app.world.seed
536	                sim_init(&app.sim, world_seed)
537	                app.screen  = .Residents
538	                app.cam_col = GRID_W / 2
539	                app.cam_row = GRID_H / 2
540	            }
541	
542	        case .Residents:
543	            if resident_list_update(&app.resident_list, &app.residents, app.engine) {
544	                creation_screen_init(&app.creation)
545	                app.screen = .Creation
546	            }
547	            sim_rect := rl.Rectangle{f32(SCREEN_W - 200), f32(SCREEN_H - 60), 180, 42}
548	            hov_sim  := rl.CheckCollisionPointRec(rl.GetMousePosition(), sim_rect)
549	            if app.residents.count > 0 {
550	                rl.DrawRectangleRec(sim_rect, hov_sim ? COL_ACCENT2 : COL_ACCENT)
551	                rl.DrawText("Simulate ->", SCREEN_W - 188, SCREEN_H - 46, UI_FSIZE, COL_TEXT)
552	                if hov_sim && rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.LEFT) {
553	                    app.screen = .Simulation
554	                    // Force immediate stat panel draw on first frame
555	                    _draw_stat_panel(app)
556	                }
557	            }
558	
559	        case .Creation:
560	            new_char: Character
561	            if creation_screen_update(&app.creation, &new_char) {
562	                app.pending_char = new_char
563	                app.pending_id   = residents_add(&app.residents, new_char)
564	                epilog_assert_character(app.engine, residents_find(&app.residents, app.pending_id))
565	                world_spawn_character(&app.world, &app.residents, app.pending_id)
566	                rel_seeding_init(&app.rel_seeding, app.pending_id, &app.residents)
567	                app.screen = .Rel_Seeding
568	            }
569	            back_rect := rl.Rectangle{f32(SCREEN_W - 130), f32(SCREEN_H - 50), 120, 36}
570	            hov_back  := rl.CheckCollisionPointRec(rl.GetMousePosition(), back_rect)
571	            rl.DrawRectangleRec(back_rect, hov_back ? COL_HOVER : COL_INPUT)
572	            rl.DrawText("<- Back", SCREEN_W - 122, SCREEN_H - 40, UI_SMALL, COL_MUTED)
573	            if hov_back && rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.LEFT) {
574	                app.screen = .Residents
575	            }
576	
577	        case .Rel_Seeding:
578	            if rel_seeding_update(&app.rel_seeding, &app.residents) {
579	                rel_seeding_commit(&app.rel_seeding, &app.residents, app.engine)

5	 * engine/epilog/epilog.dll at link time.

7	 * Usage:
8	 *   e := epilog.epilog_create()
9	 *   epilog.epilog_load_string(e, "parent(alice, bob).")
10	 *   epilog.epilog_query(e, "parent(X, Y)", my_callback, nil)

Let me think clearly: `_draw_logo_phase` returns 1 when "New Game" is clicked AND advances `t.phase` to `.Island_Name`. `_draw_name_phase` returns 1 when the name is confirmed. So result==1 from `.Logo` phase → stay on Title (phase now Island_Name). Result==1 from `.Island_Name` phase → go to World_Setup. The check should be: if we got result==1 AND phase is now `.Island_Name` (just changed), stay. If we got result==1 AND phase was already `.Island_Name` (name confirmed), go.

# DMLS — Deb's Minimal Life Simulator

> *A minimal life simulation engine. Maximal engineering underneath.*

DMLS is a 2D life simulation built on a declarative relational engine ([Epilog](engine/epilog/)), a generative spatial layer (Perlin noise, seeded PRNG), and a Raylib renderer written in Odin. Characters live on a 256×256 grid, form relationships, develop crushes, build rivalries — and you watch it unfold from outside.

---

## Stack

| Layer | Technology | Role |
|-------|-----------|------|
| Relational engine | Epilog v0.2 (C++23) | Fact storage, relationship queries, derived logic |
| Simulation & rendering | Odin + Raylib | Game loop, grid, noise, randomness, UI |
| Bridge | `extern "C"` API + Odin `foreign` | Epilog embedded as a shared library |

---

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               Raylib Window             │
│  ┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┐ │
│  │  Simulation View │  Stats Panel    │ │
│  │  (RenderTexture) │  (RenderTexture)│ │
│  └──────────────────┴─────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ Odin game loop
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           Odin Simulation Layer         │
│  Grid · Noise · Randomness · Characters │
│  Character Creation · System Manager   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
            ↕ C++↔Odin bridge
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         Epilog v0.2 (C++ module)        │
│  Facts · Rules · Queries · Memoization  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Directory Layout

```
dmls/
├── engine/
│   └── epilog/          Epilog v0.2 C++ source (self-contained module)
│       ├── include/     Public headers (epilog_ffi.h, ...)
│       ├── engine/      Solver, database, FFI, memo, stats
│       ├── parser/      Lexer + parser
│       ├── internals/   Atoms, terms, variables
│       ├── epilog.def   DLL export list (Windows)
│       ├── epilog.dll   Prebuilt Windows DLL  (regenerated by build.bat)
│       └── Makefile     Epilog standalone build (tests, Linux .so)
├── src/
│   ├── main.odin        Entry point + bridge smoke test
│   ├── bridge.odin      Odin foreign import of Epilog C API
│   ├── sim/             Simulation systems (Phase 3+)
│   ├── render/          Raylib rendering layer (Phase 6+)
│   ├── ui/              Character creation, stats panel (Phase 2+)
│   └── data/            Save/load, binary format (Phase 7+)
├── assets/              Sprites, fonts, icons
├── build/               Compiled output (gitignored)
├── build.bat            Windows build script
├── build.sh             Linux / macOS build script
├── PLAN.md              Full milestone plan
└── README.md            This file
```

---

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| [Odin](https://odin-lang.org) | nightly ≥ 2026-05 | `odin` must be on `PATH` |
| [clang++](https://clang.llvm.org) | ≥ 17 | For building the Epilog DLL/SO |
| Raylib | 5.x | Added in Phase 2 |

---

## Building

### Windows

```bat
build.bat          :: release build (DLL + Odin binary)
build.bat debug    :: debug build
build.bat engine   :: rebuild Epilog DLL only
build.bat run      :: build then run
build.bat clean    :: remove build/ artifacts
```

The script compiles Epilog to `engine/epilog/epilog.dll` (with `epilog.lib` import library), copies the DLL into `build/`, then compiles the Odin project to `build/dmls.exe`.

### Linux / macOS

```sh
chmod +x build.sh
./build.sh         # release
./build.sh debug   # debug
./build.sh engine  # Epilog .so only
./build.sh run     # build + run
./build.sh clean
```

### Running Epilog tests standalone

```sh
cd engine/epilog
make test          # compiles + runs all 10 test suites
```

---

## Milestone Status

| Milestone | Deliverable | Status |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| **M0** | Epilog v0.2 complete — indexing, memoization, C FFI | ✅ Done |
| **M1** | Odin skeleton, bridge smoke test passing | ✅ Done |
| **M2** | Character creation screen end-to-end | ✅ Done |
| **M3** | 256×256 grid with Perlin noise rendering | ✅ Done |
| **M4** | Randomness systems implemented and tested | ✅ Done |
| **M5** | Relational simulation — crushes, rivals, moods | ✅ Done |
| **M6** | Dual RenderTexture layout with stats panel | ✅ Done |
| M7 | Save/load with full state round-trip | ⬜ |
| M8 | Polish — title screen, animations, release build | ⬜ |

---

## How the Bridge Works

`src/bridge.odin` declares Odin `foreign` bindings to the Epilog C API defined in `engine/epilog/include/epilog_ffi.h`. On Windows, the Odin linker links against `epilog.lib` (an import library generated alongside `epilog.dll`). At runtime, Windows loads `epilog.dll` from the same directory as the executable.

```odin
// Assert a fact
epilog_load_string(engine, "crushing(uriel, character_a).")

// Assert a rule
epilog_load_string(engine, "rivals(X, Y) :- crushing(X, Z), crushing(Y, Z), X \\= Y.")

// Query — callback fires once per solution
epilog_query(engine, "rivals(X, Y)", my_callback, &my_ctx)
```

Epilog is always the **source of truth** for social state. Odin never caches relationship data — it queries Epilog every simulation tick. Rendering reflects queries, never assumptions.

---

## Epilog v0.2 — What's Inside

Epilog is a purpose-built Prolog-compatible relational engine in C++23.

**Phase 0.1** — Minimal runtime: atoms, variables, compound terms, unification, backtracking SLD resolution, built-ins (`true`, `fail`, `!`, `=`, `\=`, `assert`, `retract`, `write`).

**Phase 0.2** — Speed + embedding:
- **First-argument indexing** — clauses partitioned by first-arg value; ground queries skip non-matching clauses without attempting unification.
- **Memoization cache** — complete solution sets for ground queries cached and invalidated on `assert`/`retract`.
- **Query statistics** — per-predicate `call_count` / `soln_count` for future predictive execution.
- **C FFI** (`epilog_ffi.h`) — pure C header, opaque engine handle, callback-based solution enumeration.

**Test suite**: 10 suites, 127 tests, all passing.

---

## Core Invariant

> The Epilog engine is always the source of truth for social state.  
> Odin never caches relationship data — it queries Epilog every tick.  
> Rendering reflects queries, never assumptions.

/*
 * starter_chars.odin — Pre-programmed starter characters (CHARACTERS.MD).
 *
 * Four characters are asserted into Epilog and placed on the grid at world
 * initialisation, before the player adds anyone via the creation screen.
 *
 * Initialisation order follows CHARACTERS.MD §Initialisation Order:
 *   1. character/2
 *   2. gender/2, dating_pref/2, pronouns/2, birthday/3, age/2
 *   3. personality_trait/2
 *   4. real_world_family/2
 *   5. nickname_for/3
 *   6. starting relationship facts (crush, friend, acquaintance, stranger, sibling)
 *   7. derived rules (see below — replace engine rules loaded at startup)
 *   8-10. interaction_count priming
 *
 * Predicate names used here follow CHARACTERS.MD exactly:
 *   crush/2, friend/2, acquaintance/2, sibling/2, stranger/2
 * The derived rules in CHARACTERS.MD use crush/2; the sim also queries
 * crushing/2 (aliased below: crushing(X,Y) :- crush(X,Y).).
 */

package dmls

import "core:fmt"
import "core:strings"

// ---- Character IDs (fixed, reserved) ---------------------------------------

STARTER_ID_CHARACTER_A :: u32(1)
STARTER_ID_URIEL     :: u32(2)
STARTER_ID_ANNA      :: u32(3)
STARTER_ID_SALONI    :: u32(4)
STARTER_COUNT        :: 4

// ---- Helper: load a single fact string into Epilog -------------------------

_sl :: proc(engine: ^EpilogEngine, fact: string) {
    buf: [512]u8
    s := fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "%s.", fact)
    buf[len(s)] = 0
    epilog_load_string(engine, cstring(raw_data(buf[:])))
}

// ---- Helper: build a Character struct from literal values ------------------

_make_char :: proc(
    id         : u32,
    name       : string,
    nickname   : string,
    age        : u8,
    gender     : Gender,
    pref       : DatingPref,
    pronouns   : Pronouns,
    personality: Personality,
    sprite     : u32,
) -> Character {
    c: Character
    c.id          = id
    c.age         = age
    c.gender      = gender
    c.dating_pref = pref
    c.pronouns    = pronouns
    c.personality = personality
    c.sprite      = sprite
    n := min(len(name), MAX_NAME_LEN - 1)
    copy(c.name[:], name[:n])
    if len(nickname) > 0 {
        nn := min(len(nickname), MAX_NAME_LEN - 1)
        copy(c.nickname[:], nickname[:nn])
    }
    return c
}

_assert_starter_facts :: proc(engine: ^EpilogEngine,

    personality_a : string,
    gender_a  : string,
    pref_a    : string,
    pronouns_a: string,
    bday_m, bday_d: int,
    age_v     : int,
    traits    : []string,
    rwf       : string,

    buf: [256]u8

    s := fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "character(%s, %s)", atom, personality_a)

    // 2. gender, dating_pref, pronouns, birthday, age
    s = fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "gender(%s, %s)", atom, gender_a)
    _sl(engine, string(buf[:len(s)]))

    s = fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "dating_pref(%s, %s)", atom, pref_a)
    _sl(engine, string(buf[:len(s)]))

    s = fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "pronouns(%s, %s)", atom, pronouns_a)
    _sl(engine, string(buf[:len(s)]))

    s = fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "birthday(%s, %d, %d)", atom, bday_m, bday_d)
    _sl(engine, string(buf[:len(s)]))

    s = fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "age(%s, %d)", atom, age_v)
    _sl(engine, string(buf[:len(s)]))

    // 3. personality_trait/2
    for t in traits {
        s = fmt.bprintf(buf[:], "personality_trait(%s, %s)", atom, t)

    }

}

// ---- Load CHARACTERS.MD derived rules (replaces engine defaults) -----------

starter_load_rules :: proc(engine: ^EpilogEngine) {
    // crush/2 alias → crushing/2 so sim tick queries work
    epilog_load_string(engine,
        "crushing(X, Y) :- crush(X, Y).")

    // rivals: two characters crushing on the same target
    epilog_load_string(engine,
        "rivals(X, Y) :- crush(X, Z), crush(Y, Z), X \\= Y.")

    // can_crush: eligible to develop a crush
    epilog_load_string(engine,
        "can_crush(X, Y) :- dating_pref(X, Pref), gender(Y, Pref), \\+ sibling(X, Y), \\+ partner(X, _), X \\= Y.")
    epilog_load_string(engine,
        "can_crush(X, Y) :- dating_pref(X, any), \\+ sibling(X, Y), \\+ partner(X, _), X \\= Y.")

    // eligible/2 used by sim_tick → delegates to can_crush
    epilog_load_string(engine,
        "eligible(X, Y) :- can_crush(X, Y).")

    // mood derivation

        "mood(X, jealous)    :- rivals(X, _).")
    epilog_load_string(engine,
        "mood(X, lovestruck) :- crush(X, _), \\+ rivals(X, _).")
    epilog_load_string(engine,

        "great_friends(X, Y) :- friend(X, Y), friend(Y, X), interaction_count(X, Y, N), N > 10.")

        "best_friends(X, Y) :- great_friends(X, Y).")

    epilog_load_string(engine,
        "unrequited(X, Y) :- crush(X, Y), \\+ crush(Y, X).")

    epilog_load_string(engine,

        "Saloni", "",
        20, .Female, .Male, .She_Her, .Outgoing_Merrymaker, 3)

    for i in 0..<STARTER_COUNT {

        res.chars[idx] = chars[i]

    }
    res.next_id = STARTER_COUNT + 1

    // ---- Assert Epilog facts (initialisation order) ------------------------

    // [NAME]
    _assert_starter_facts(engine, "character_a",
        "ambitious_achiever", "male", "any", "he_him",
        6, 15, 20,
        []string{"confident", "straight_talker", "results_driven"},
        "yes")

    // Uriel
    _assert_starter_facts(engine, "uriel",
        "outgoing_merrymaker", "female", "any", "she_her",
        6, 20, 21,
        []string{"cheerful", "infectiously_positive", "socially_confident"},
        "yes")

    // Anna Croft
    _assert_starter_facts(engine, "anna_croft",
        "outgoing_dynamo", "female", "male", "she_her",
        7, 12, 21,
        []string{"energetic", "driven", "action_oriented"},
        "no")

    // Saloni
    _assert_starter_facts(engine, "saloni",
        "outgoing_merrymaker", "female", "male", "she_her",
        7, 18, 20,

    _sl(engine, "nickname_for(anna_croft, character_a, sunflower)")
    _sl(engine, "nickname_for(character_a, anna_croft, my_demon)")

    _sl(engine, "sibling(character_a, saloni)")
    _sl(engine, "sibling(saloni, character_a)")
    _sl(engine, "crush(character_a, uriel)")
    _sl(engine, "friend(character_a, uriel)")
    _sl(engine, "friend(character_a, saloni)")
    _sl(engine, "acquaintance(character_a, anna_croft)")
    //    Also load as relationship/3 for the residents screen queries
    _sl(engine, "relationship(character_a, saloni, sibling)")
    _sl(engine, "relationship(character_a, uriel, friend)")
    _sl(engine, "relationship(character_a, anna_croft, acquaintance)")

    //    Uriel
    _sl(engine, "crush(uriel, character_a)")
    _sl(engine, "friend(uriel, character_a)")
    _sl(engine, "acquaintance(uriel, saloni)")
    _sl(engine, "stranger(uriel, anna_croft)")
    _sl(engine, "relationship(uriel, character_a, friend)")
    _sl(engine, "relationship(uriel, saloni, acquaintance)")

    //    Anna Croft
    _sl(engine, "acquaintance(anna_croft, character_a)")
    _sl(engine, "stranger(anna_croft, saloni)")
    _sl(engine, "stranger(anna_croft, uriel)")
    _sl(engine, "relationship(anna_croft, character_a, acquaintance)")

    //    Saloni
    _sl(engine, "friend(saloni, character_a)")
    _sl(engine, "acquaintance(saloni, uriel)")
    _sl(engine, "stranger(saloni, anna_croft)")
    _sl(engine, "relationship(saloni, character_a, friend)")
    _sl(engine, "relationship(saloni, character_a, sibling)")
    _sl(engine, "relationship(saloni, uriel, acquaintance)")

    // 8-10. Primed interaction counts
    _sl(engine, "interaction_count(character_a, uriel, 5)")
    _sl(engine, "interaction_count(character_a, saloni, 20)")
    _sl(engine, "interaction_count(character_a, anna_croft, 2)")

    // ---- Spawn on grid -----------------------------------------------------

    // Starters spawn in their designated zones.
    // We try the preferred zone first; grid_find_spawn falls back automatically.
    _spawn_in_zone(world, res, STARTER_ID_CHARACTER_A, .Town)
    _spawn_in_zone(world, res, STARTER_ID_URIEL,     .Beach)
    _spawn_in_zone(world, res, STARTER_ID_ANNA,      .Grass)
    _spawn_in_zone(world, res, STARTER_ID_SALONI,    .Town)
}

// Attempt to spawn a character in a preferred terrain zone.
// Falls back to any spawnable cell if the preferred zone is not found quickly.
_spawn_in_zone :: proc(world: ^World, res: ^Residents, id: u32, preferred: Terrain) {
    c := residents_find(res, id)
    if c == nil do return

    // Try up to 256 times to find a cell of the preferred terrain.
    for _ in 0..<256 {
        world.rng = world.rng * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
        col := i32((world.rng >> 33) % GRID_W)
        world.rng = world.rng * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
        row := i32((world.rng >> 17) % GRID_H)
        cell := &world.grid.cells[row][col]
        if cell.terrain == preferred && cell.occupant == 0 {
            if grid_place_character(&world.grid, id, col, row) {
                c.position = {col, row}
                idx := int(id - 1)
                if idx < MAX_RESIDENTS { world.positions[idx] = c.position }
                return
            }
        }
    }

    // Fallback: any spawnable cell
    col, row, ok := grid_find_spawn(&world.grid, &world.rng)
    if ok {
        grid_place_character(&world.grid, id, col, row)
        c.position = {col, row}
        idx := int(id - 1)
        if idx < MAX_RESIDENTS { world.positions[idx] = c.position }
    }
}

    _spawn_in_zone(world, res, STARTER_ID_SALONI,    .Town)
}

// Attempt to spawn a character in a preferred terrain zone.
// Falls back to any spawnable cell if the preferred zone is not found quickly.
_spawn_in_zone :: proc(world: ^World, res: ^Residents, id: u32, preferred: Terrain) {
    c := residents_find(res, id)
    if c == nil do return

    // Try up to 256 times to find a cell of the preferred terrain.
    for _ in 0..<256 {
        world.rng = world.rng * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
        col := i32((world.rng >> 33) % GRID_W)
        world.rng = world.rng * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
        row := i32((world.rng >> 17) % GRID_H)
        cell := &world.grid.cells[row][col]
        if cell.terrain == preferred && cell.occupant == 0 {
            if grid_place_character(&world.grid, id, col, row) {
                c.position = {col, row}
                idx := int(id - 1)
                if idx < MAX_RESIDENTS { world.positions[idx] = c.position }
                return
            }
        }
    }

    // Fallback: any spawnable cell
    col, row, ok := grid_find_spawn(&world.grid, &world.rng)
    if ok {
        grid_place_character(&world.grid, id, col, row)
        c.position = {col, row}
        idx := int(id - 1)
        if idx < MAX_RESIDENTS { world.positions[idx] = c.position }
    }
}

Now I understand the full picture. The plan:

1. **`screen_cfg.odin`** — `ScreenConfig` struct with runtime `W`, `H`; a `ScreenSize` enum; resolution picker added to the title screen (before island name).
2. **`creation.odin`** — change `SCREEN_W/H` from compile-time constants to runtime values read from a global `g_screen`. All UI procs that use `SCREEN_W/H` will use `g_screen.w/h` instead. 
3. **Character colours** — define a fixed palette of 8 distinct colours indexed by `c.sprite`, and replace the hue-formula colour in `_char_color` and stat panel.
4. **Starter characters** already have `sprite` 0–3 set — those will map to their canonical colours.

The tricky part: `SCREEN_W` and `SCREEN_H` are compile-time constants used in many places. The cleanest approach for Odin is to keep the constants as the **maximum** values and use a global `g_screen` struct for the active resolution — all rendering procs use `g_screen.w/h`, `rl.SetWindowSize` is called when the player picks a resolution.

   - **Odin language**: single-package flat layout, `#force_inline proc`, struct literals use `field = value` (NOT `field: value`), `for i, v in slice` gives value first then index (opposite of Go), XOR-assign is `~=`, `fmt.bprintf` takes `[]byte` and returns written `string`

   - **Raylib RenderTexture2D**: Y-flipped, must use `DrawTexturePro` with negative source height to composite correctly; allocated at max size (SCREEN_W×SCREEN_H), composited at runtime resolution
   - **Runtime screen config**: `g_screen` global, `SW()/SH()` inline procs, `stats_x()/sim_w()/sim_h()/stat_w()/stat_h()` layout procs — all rendering uses these instead of compile-time `SCREEN_W/H`

   - **PCG-style DependentRNG**: state+seq fields, `dependent_next_u64` via xorshift, survives save/load
   - **CRC-32 IEEE 802.3**: table-based, computed over all save bytes before checksum field
   - **Character palette**: 8 fixed colours indexed by `c.sprite` (0=[NAME] amber, 1=Uriel sky blue, 2=Anna coral red, 3=Saloni peach, 4-7 for player chars)

1	/*
2	 * screen_cfg.odin — Runtime screen resolution configuration.
3	 *
4	 * Three supported resolutions: 640×320, 1920×720, 1920×1080.
5	 * The player picks one on the title screen before generating the world.
6	 *
7	 * SCREEN_W / SCREEN_H compile-time constants remain as the maximum dimensions
8	 * (1920×1080) used only for RenderTexture allocation and rl.InitWindow.
9	 * All rendering code reads SW() / SH() for the active dimensions.
10	 *
11	 * Derived layout values (stats panel split, sim panel dimensions) are also
12	 * exposed as procs so they react to resolution changes automatically.
13	 */
14	
15	package dmls
16	
17	import rl "vendor:raylib"
18	
19	// ---- Resolution enum -------------------------------------------------------
20	
21	ScreenSize :: enum {
22	    S_640x320,
23	    S_1920x720,
24	    S_1920x1080,
25	}
26	
27	SCREEN_SIZE_LABELS := [ScreenSize]cstring{
28	    .S_640x320   = "640 × 320  (Compact)",
29	    .S_1920x720  = "1920 × 720  (Wide)",
30	    .S_1920x1080 = "1920 × 1080  (Full HD)",
31	}
32	
33	SCREEN_SIZE_W := [ScreenSize]i32{
34	    .S_640x320   = 640,
35	    .S_1920x720  = 1920,
36	    .S_1920x1080 = 1920,
37	}
38	
39	SCREEN_SIZE_H := [ScreenSize]i32{
40	    .S_640x320   = 320,
41	    .S_1920x720  = 720,
42	    .S_1920x1080 = 1080,
43	}
44	
45	// ---- Active screen state (global) -----------------------------------------
46	
47	ScreenCfg :: struct {
48	    w    : i32,
49	    h    : i32,
50	    size : ScreenSize,
51	}
52	
53	g_screen : ScreenCfg
54	
55	screen_cfg_set :: proc(sz: ScreenSize) {
56	    g_screen.size = sz
57	    g_screen.w    = SCREEN_SIZE_W[sz]
58	    g_screen.h    = SCREEN_SIZE_H[sz]
59	    rl.SetWindowSize(g_screen.w, g_screen.h)
60	}
61	
62	// Convenience accessors used everywhere in rendering code.
63	SW :: #force_inline proc() -> i32 { return g_screen.w }
64	SH :: #force_inline proc() -> i32 { return g_screen.h }
65	
66	// Derived layout values — all relative to active resolution.
67	stats_x  :: #force_inline proc() -> i32 { return SW() * 55 / 100 }
68	sim_w    :: #force_inline proc() -> i32 { return stats_x() }
69	sim_h    :: #force_inline proc() -> i32 { return SH() }
70	stat_w   :: #force_inline proc() -> i32 { return SW() - stats_x() }
71	stat_h   :: #force_inline proc() -> i32 { return SH() }

73	// ---- Character colour palette (8 distinct colours, indexed by sprite) ------
74	//
75	// Each of the 8 sprite slots has a fixed canonical colour.
76	// Starter characters are assigned slots 0–3 matching their canonical look.
77	//   0 = [NAME] — warm amber / gold

79	//   2 = Anna Croft — vivid coral red
80	//   3 = Saloni    — peach / warm orange
81	//   4–7           — available for player-created characters

83	CHAR_PALETTE := [SPRITE_COUNT]rl.Color{
84	    rl.Color{230, 180,  60, 255},  // 0 [NAME]  — amber gold
85	    rl.Color{ 80, 180, 230, 255},  // 1 Uriel       — sky blue
86	    rl.Color{220,  70,  70, 255},  // 2 Anna Croft  — coral red
87	    rl.Color{240, 150,  80, 255},  // 3 Saloni      — warm peach
88	    rl.Color{100, 210, 140, 255},  // 4              — mint green
89	    rl.Color{170,  90, 220, 255},  // 5              — violet
90	    rl.Color{220, 210,  80, 255},  // 6              — yellow

92	}

94	char_palette_color :: proc(sprite: u32) -> rl.Color {
95	    idx := int(sprite) % SPRITE_COUNT
96	    return CHAR_PALETTE[idx]

98	
99	// ---- Resolution picker UI --------------------------------------------------
100	// Drawn on the title screen before island naming.
101	// Returns true when the player has confirmed a choice.
102	
103	ResolutionPicker :: struct {
104	    chosen   : ScreenSize,
105	    confirmed: bool,
106	}
107	
108	resolution_picker_init :: proc(p: ^ResolutionPicker) {
109	    p.chosen    = .S_1920x1080
110	    p.confirmed = false
111	}
112	
113	// Draw and handle input. Returns true once confirmed.
114	resolution_picker_update :: proc(p: ^ResolutionPicker) -> bool {
115	    rl.ClearBackground(COL_BG)
116	
117	    cy := SH() / 2 - 120
118	    rl.DrawText("Choose resolution", UI_LPAD, cy - 40, UI_HSIZE, COL_TEXT)
119	
120	    for sz in ScreenSize {
121	        label := SCREEN_SIZE_LABELS[sz]
122	        sel   := p.chosen == sz
123	        rect  := rl.Rectangle{f32(UI_LPAD), f32(cy), 400, 44}
124	        bg    := sel ? COL_SELECT : COL_INPUT
125	        hov   := rl.CheckCollisionPointRec(rl.GetMousePosition(), rect)
126	        if hov { bg = sel ? COL_ACCENT : COL_HOVER }
127	        rl.DrawRectangleRec(rect, bg)
128	        rl.DrawRectangleLinesEx(rect, 1, sel ? COL_ACCENT : COL_MUTED)
129	        rl.DrawText(label, UI_LPAD + 14, cy + 12, UI_FSIZE, COL_TEXT)
130	        if hov && rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.LEFT) {
131	            p.chosen = sz
132	        }
133	        cy += 54
134	    }
135	
136	    cy += 10
137	    ok_rect := rl.Rectangle{f32(UI_LPAD), f32(cy), 200, 44}
138	    hov_ok  := rl.CheckCollisionPointRec(rl.GetMousePosition(), ok_rect)
139	    rl.DrawRectangleRec(ok_rect, hov_ok ? COL_ACCENT : COL_SELECT)
140	    rl.DrawText("Confirm ->", UI_LPAD + 16, cy + 12, UI_FSIZE, COL_TEXT)
141	
142	    if (hov_ok && rl.IsMouseButtonPressed(.LEFT)) || rl.IsKeyPressed(.ENTER) {
143	        screen_cfg_set(p.chosen)
144	        p.confirmed = true
145	        return true
146	    }
147	    return false
148	}

1	/*
2	 * grid.odin — 256×256 world grid (M3).
3	 *
4	 * Each cell stores a terrain type, occupant character id (0 = empty),
5	 * and a generic object id (0 = none).
6	 *
7	 * Terrain zones and their walkability:
8	 *   .Water  — impassable
9	 *   .Beach  — walkable, spawnable
10	 *   .Grass  — walkable, spawnable
11	 *   .Town   — walkable, spawnable (preferred spawn)
12	 *   .Forest — walkable, not spawnable
13	 */
14	
15	package dmls
16	
17	import rl "vendor:raylib"
18	import "core:math"
19	
20	GRID_W :: 256
21	GRID_H :: 256
22	
23	// Terrain scale: smaller = more zoomed-out noise features.
24	TERRAIN_SCALE :: 0.035
25	TERRAIN_OCTAVES :: 5
26	
27	Terrain :: enum u8 {
28	    Water,
29	    Beach,
30	    Grass,
31	    Town,
32	    Forest,
33	}
34	
35	Cell :: struct {
36	    terrain   : Terrain,
37	    occupant  : u32,    // character id, 0 = empty
38	    object_id : u32,    // reserved for Phase 8 objects
39	}
40	
41	Grid :: struct {
42	    cells     : [GRID_H][GRID_W]Cell,
43	    world_seed: u64,
44	}
45	
46	// ---- Terrain colour lookup -------------------------------------------------
47	
48	terrain_color :: proc(t: Terrain) -> rl.Color {
49	    switch t {
50	    case .Water:  return rl.Color{30,  80,  160, 255}
51	    case .Beach:  return rl.Color{210, 190, 130, 255}
52	    case .Grass:  return rl.Color{60,  140, 60,  255}
53	    case .Town:   return rl.Color{160, 140, 110, 255}
54	    case .Forest: return rl.Color{30,  90,  30,  255}
55	    }
56	    return rl.Color{0, 0, 0, 255}
57	}
58	
59	terrain_walkable :: proc(t: Terrain) -> bool {
60	    return t != .Water
61	}
62	
63	terrain_spawnable :: proc(t: Terrain) -> bool {
64	    return t == .Grass || t == .Town || t == .Beach
65	}
66	
67	// ---- Grid generation -------------------------------------------------------
68	
69	grid_generate :: proc(g: ^Grid, seed: u64) {
70	    g.world_seed = seed
71	    g^ = {}
72	    g.world_seed = seed
73	
74	    ns: NoiseState
75	    noise_init(&ns, seed)
76	
77	    // Second noise for town/forest layer
78	    ns2: NoiseState
79	    noise_init(&ns2, seed ~ 0xdeadbeefcafe1234)
80	
81	    for row in 0..<GRID_H {
82	        for col in 0..<GRID_W {
83	            x := f64(col)
84	            y := f64(row)
85	
86	            // Island mask: distance from centre falls off to water at edges
87	            cx  := f64(GRID_W) / 2.0
88	            cy  := f64(GRID_H) / 2.0
89	            dx  := (x - cx) / cx
90	            dy  := (y - cy) / cy
91	            dist := math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
92	
93	            // Base elevation from fBm noise
94	            elevation := fbm(&ns, x * TERRAIN_SCALE, y * TERRAIN_SCALE, TERRAIN_OCTAVES)
95	            // Clamp to [-1,1] roughly — fBm with 5 octaves goes beyond 1
96	            elevation = elevation * 0.5
97	
98	            // Apply island radial mask — edges become water
99	            elevation -= dist * 1.2
100	
101	            // Secondary noise for town/forest differentiation
102	            detail := perlin2(&ns2, x * TERRAIN_SCALE * 2, y * TERRAIN_SCALE * 2)
103	
104	            terrain: Terrain
105	            switch {
106	            case elevation < -0.3:
107	                terrain = .Water
108	            case elevation < -0.1:
109	                terrain = .Beach
110	            case elevation < 0.25:
111	                // Grass vs town vs forest based on detail noise
112	                if detail > 0.3 {
113	                    terrain = .Town
114	                } else if detail < -0.3 {
115	                    terrain = .Forest
116	                } else {
117	                    terrain = .Grass
118	                }
119	            case:
120	                terrain = .Forest   // high ground = dense forest
121	            }
122	
123	            g.cells[row][col].terrain = terrain
124	        }
125	    }
126	}
127	
128	// ---- Occupant helpers ------------------------------------------------------
129	
130	grid_place_character :: proc(g: ^Grid, id: u32, col, row: i32) -> bool {
131	    if col < 0 || col >= GRID_W || row < 0 || row >= GRID_H do return false
132	    cell := &g.cells[row][col]
133	    if cell.occupant != 0 do return false
134	    if !terrain_walkable(cell.terrain) do return false
135	    cell.occupant = id
136	    return true
137	}
138	
139	grid_move_character :: proc(g: ^Grid, id: u32, old_col, old_row, new_col, new_row: i32) -> bool {
140	    if new_col < 0 || new_col >= GRID_W || new_row < 0 || new_row >= GRID_H do return false
141	    dst := &g.cells[new_row][new_col]
142	    if dst.occupant != 0 do return false
143	    if !terrain_walkable(dst.terrain) do return false
144	    g.cells[old_row][old_col].occupant = 0
145	    dst.occupant = id
146	    return true
147	}
148	
149	grid_remove_character :: proc(g: ^Grid, col, row: i32) {
150	    if col >= 0 && col < GRID_W && row >= 0 && row < GRID_H {
151	        g.cells[row][col].occupant = 0
152	    }
153	}
154	
155	// ---- Spawn: find a random spawnable cell using a simple LCG ----------------
156	
157	grid_find_spawn :: proc(g: ^Grid, rng: ^u64) -> (col, row: i32, ok: bool) {
158	    for _ in 0..<512 {
159	        rng^ = rng^ * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
160	        c := i32((rng^ >> 33) % GRID_W)
161	        r := i32((rng^ >> 17) % GRID_H)
162	        cell := &g.cells[r][c]
163	        if terrain_spawnable(cell.terrain) && cell.occupant == 0 {
164	            return c, r, true
165	        }
166	    }
167	    return 0, 0, false
168	}
169	
170	// ---- Rendering -------------------------------------------------------------
171	
172	// cell_px — pixel size when rendering at the given zoom.
173	RENDER_CELL_PX :: 3   // each grid cell = 3×3 pixels
174	
175	// Render the grid into the current drawing context.
176	// origin_x/y: top-left pixel of the simulation view.
177	// view_w/h:   pixel size of the simulation panel.
178	grid_render :: proc(g: ^Grid, origin_x, origin_y, view_w, view_h: i32,
179	                    cam_col, cam_row: i32) {
180	    visible_cols := view_w  / RENDER_CELL_PX + 2
181	    visible_rows := view_h / RENDER_CELL_PX + 2
182	
183	    start_col := cam_col - visible_cols / 2
184	    start_row := cam_row - visible_rows / 2
185	
186	    for r in 0..<visible_rows {
187	        for c in 0..<visible_cols {
188	            gc := start_col + c
189	            gr := start_row + r
190	            if gc < 0 || gc >= GRID_W || gr < 0 || gr >= GRID_H do continue
191	
192	            cell  := &g.cells[gr][gc]
193	            color := terrain_color(cell.terrain)
194	
195	            px := origin_x + c * RENDER_CELL_PX
196	            py := origin_y + r * RENDER_CELL_PX
197	            rl.DrawRectangle(px, py, RENDER_CELL_PX, RENDER_CELL_PX, color)
198	
199	            // Draw occupant dot
200	            if cell.occupant != 0 {
201	                dot_x := px + RENDER_CELL_PX / 2
202	                dot_y := py + RENDER_CELL_PX / 2
203	                rl.DrawPixel(dot_x, dot_y, rl.WHITE)
204	            }
205	        }
206	    }
207	}
208

1	/*
2	 * main.odin — DMLS entry point (M0–M8, complete).
3	 *
4	 * Screen state machine:
5	 *   .Title        — animated title card + New/Load buttons           (M8)
6	 *   .Island_Name  — name-your-island input                           (M8)
7	 *   .World_Setup  — hex seed entry, generate island
8	 *   .Residents    — resident list + "Add resident"
9	 *   .Creation     — character creation form
10	 *   .Rel_Seeding  — relationship tags for new character
11	 *   .Simulation   — dual RenderTexture: grid + stats panel           (M6)
12	 *

15	 *   Right stat_tex (45%): island stats, residents, crushes, events
16	 *   Both redrawn at appropriate rates; composited with DrawTexturePro.
17	 *

19	 * Cutscene overlay (M8): triggered by new social events from SimState.

97	_parse_seed :: proc(s: string) -> (u64, bool) {

99	    if len(s) == 0 do return 0, false
100	    for ch in s {
101	        switch ch {
102	        case '0'..='9': val = val * 16 + u64(ch - '0')
103	        case 'a'..='f': val = val * 16 + u64(ch - 'a' + 10)
104	        case 'A'..='F': val = val * 16 + u64(ch - 'A' + 10)

106	        }

209	// ---- Grid-to-screen coordinate mapping ------------------------------------
210	
211	_grid_to_screen :: proc(gc, gr, cam_col, cam_row, view_w, view_h: i32) -> (px, py: i32, visible: bool) {
212	    visible_cols := view_w  / RENDER_CELL_PX + 2
213	    visible_rows := view_h / RENDER_CELL_PX + 2
214	    start_col    := cam_col - visible_cols / 2
215	    start_row    := cam_row - visible_rows / 2
216	    dc           := gc - start_col
217	    dr           := gr - start_row
218	    if dc < 0 || dc >= visible_cols || dr < 0 || dr >= visible_rows {
219	        return 0, 0, false
220	    }
221	    return dc * RENDER_CELL_PX, dr * RENDER_CELL_PX, true
222	}

224	// ---- Hover arrow query (c-callback, no context) ----------------------------
225	
226	_HoverRelAccum :: struct {
227	    ids   : [MAX_RESIDENTS]u32,
228	    count : int,
229	}
230	
231	_hover_rel_cb :: proc "c" (soln: ^EpilogSolution, ud: rawptr) -> EpilogSignal {
232	    acc := cast(^_HoverRelAccum)ud
233	    if acc.count >= MAX_RESIDENTS do return .EPILOG_STOP
234	    for i in 0..<epilog_soln_var_count(soln) {
235	        name := epilog_soln_var_name(soln, i)
236	        val  := epilog_soln_var_atom(soln, i)
237	        if name == nil || val == nil do continue
238	        if string(name) == "Other" {
239	            other_str := string(val)
240	            other_id  := u32(0)
241	            if len(other_str) > 5 && other_str[:5] == "char_" {
242	                for ch in other_str[5:] {
243	                    if ch >= '0' && ch <= '9' {
244	                        other_id = other_id * 10 + u32(ch - '0')
245	                    }
246	                }
247	            }
248	            acc.ids[acc.count] = other_id
249	            acc.count += 1
250	        }
251	    }
252	    return .EPILOG_NEXT
253	}

255	_draw_hover_arrows :: proc(app: ^App, hovered_char: ^Character) {
256	    buf_id, goal_buf: [128]u8
257	    atom := character_atom(hovered_char.id, buf_id[:])
258	    gs   := fmt.bprintf(goal_buf[:], "relationship(%s, Other, _)", atom)
259	    goal_buf[len(gs)] = 0
260	
261	    acc := _HoverRelAccum{}
262	    epilog_query(app.engine, cstring(raw_data(goal_buf[:])), _hover_rel_cb, &acc)
263	
264	    hx, hy, hv := _grid_to_screen(hovered_char.position[0], hovered_char.position[1],
265	                                   app.cam_col, app.cam_row, sim_w(), sim_h())
266	    if !hv do return
267	
268	    for i in 0..<acc.count {
269	        other := residents_find(&app.residents, acc.ids[i])
270	        if other == nil do continue
271	        ox, oy, ov := _grid_to_screen(other.position[0], other.position[1],
272	                                       app.cam_col, app.cam_row, sim_w(), sim_h())
273	        if !ov do continue
274	        rl.DrawLine(hx + RENDER_CELL_PX/2, hy + RENDER_CELL_PX/2,
275	                    ox + RENDER_CELL_PX/2, oy + RENDER_CELL_PX/2,
276	                    rl.Color{200, 200, 60, 160})
277	    }
278	}

465	// ---- Simulation update + composite -----------------------------------------
466	
467	_update_simulation :: proc(app: ^App) {
468	    dt := rl.GetFrameTime()
469	    app.anim_time += dt
470	
471	    // WASD pan
472	    if rl.IsKeyDown(.W) { app.cam_row -= 2 }
473	    if rl.IsKeyDown(.S) { app.cam_row += 2 }
474	    if rl.IsKeyDown(.A) { app.cam_col -= 2 }
475	    if rl.IsKeyDown(.D) { app.cam_col += 2 }
476	    app.cam_col = clamp(app.cam_col, 0, GRID_W - 1)
477	    app.cam_row = clamp(app.cam_row, 0, GRID_H - 1)
478	
479	    // F5 = save, F9 = load
480	    if rl.IsKeyPressed(.F5) {
481	        _do_save(app)
482	    }
483	    if rl.IsKeyPressed(.F9) {
484	        if _do_load(app) {
485	            _draw_stat_panel(app)
486	        }
487	    }
488	
489	    // Sim tick at 1 Hz
490	    app.sim_timer += dt
491	    if app.sim_timer >= 1.0 {
492	        app.sim_timer = 0
493	        world_tick_wander(&app.world, &app.residents)
494	        sim_tick(&app.sim, &app.residents, app.engine, app.world.tick)
495	        _check_cutscene(app)
496	
497	        // Auto-save every 60 ticks
498	        if app.world.tick - app.last_autosave_tick >= 60 {
499	            _do_save(app)
500	            app.last_autosave_tick = app.world.tick
501	        }
502	    }
503	
504	    // Draw at rate
505	    _draw_sim_view(app)
506	    app.stat_timer += dt
507	    if app.stat_timer >= STAT_RATE {
508	        app.stat_timer = 0
509	        _draw_stat_panel(app)
510	    }
511	
512	    // Composite
513	    rl.ClearBackground(rl.BLACK)
514	
515	    src_sim  := rl.Rectangle{0, 0, f32(sim_w()), -f32(sim_h())}
516	    dst_sim  := rl.Rectangle{0, 0, f32(sim_w()),  f32(sim_h())}
517	    rl.DrawTexturePro(app.sim_tex.texture, src_sim, dst_sim, {0, 0}, 0, rl.WHITE)
518	
519	    src_stat := rl.Rectangle{0, 0, f32(stat_w()), -f32(stat_h())}
520	    dst_stat := rl.Rectangle{f32(stats_x()), 0, f32(stat_w()), f32(stat_h())}
521	    rl.DrawTexturePro(app.stat_tex.texture, src_stat, dst_stat, {0, 0}, 0, rl.WHITE)
522	
523	    rl.DrawLine(stats_x(), 0, stats_x(), SH(), COL_MUTED)
524	
525	    _handle_stat_clicks(app)
526	
527	    // M8 cutscene overlay on top of everything
528	    cutscene_update(&app.cutscene)
529	}
